             cleared to ‘0’, then the controller associated with this data structure was not suspended for the entire

5.2.20.1.2 Get Exported NVM Subsystem State (Management Operation 1h)
The Get Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation of the Migration Receive command allows
the host to retrieve state data for the Exported NVM Subsystem specified by the in the Exported NVM
Subsystem Identifier field in the Management Operation Specific field (refer to Figure 417Figure 417). The
data structure returned in the data buffer is the Exported NVM Subsystem state data defined by the



                                                                 429
                                                            NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


Exported NVM Subsystem Template specified by the Exported NVM Subsystem Template Index field in
the Command Dword 11 field as defined by Figure 418Figure 418.
If the Underlying Controllers associated with the specified Exported NVM Subsystem:
    •    are suspended (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1); and
    •    remains suspended during the processing of the Migration Receive command,
then:
    •    those Underlying Controllers have stopped processing commands; and
    •    if:
             o    a Controller Level Reset has not occurred on any of those Underlying Controllers during
                  the processing of the Migration Receive command; or
             o    the host does not modify controller properties on any of the Underlying Controllers during
                  the processing of the Migration Receive command,
         then the returned Exported NVM Subsystem State data structure is consistent between each field
         reported in that data structure.
If any Underlying Controller associated with the specified Exported NVM Subsystem:
    •    is not suspended during the processing of the Migration Receive command; or
    •    has a Controller Level Reset occur during the processing of the Migration Receive command,
then the Exported NVM Subsystem state may be changing during the processing of the Migration Receive
command and:
    •    each field in the reported Exported NVM Subsystem state contains the value that reflects the state
         of the specified Exported NVM Subsystem at the time the value was obtained by the controller
         processing the Migration Receive command; and
    •    state of the specified Exported NVM Subsystem may be in a different state between different fields
         (i.e., the returned Exported NVM Subsystem state may or may not be internally consistent between
         each field).
The Get Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation uses the Management Operation Specific
field as defined in Figure 417Figure 417.

         Figure 417: Get Exported NVM Subsystem State – Management Operation Specific

5.2.21 Migration Send command
The Migration Send command is used to manage the migration of a controller (refer to section 8.1.14) or
the migration of an Exported NVM Subsystem (refer to section 8.1.11.2.3.2).
The Migration Send command uses the Command Dword 10 field and Command Dword 14 field. The use
of the Data Pointer field, Command Dword 11 field, Command Dword 12 field, Command Dword 13 field,
and Command Dword 15 field is specific to the management operation specified by the Select field . All
other command specific fields are reserved.
The Select field defined in Figure 421Figure 421 specifies the management operation to be performed.
Refer to section 5.2.21.1 for a description of each management operation.




                                                               431
                                                                   NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4



                              Figure 421: Migration Send – Command Dword 10
 Bits     Description
          Management Operation Specific (MOS): The definition of this field is specific to a management operation

          reserved.
 15:08    Reserved
          Select (SEL): This field specifies the type of management operation to perform.
                             Value       Management Operation                     Reference Section
                                0h       Suspend                                      5.2.21.2.1

           Host Migration of State Data
The host may submit one or more Migration Send commands to transfer state data as defined by the
management operation (refer to the Select field in Figure 421Figure 421). If more than one Migration Send
command is submitted to transfer the state data, then:
    •     The host first submits a Migration Send command with:
              o   the Select field set to the appropriate management operation (e.g., Set Controller State
                  (i.e., 2h) or Set Exported NVM Subsystem State (i.e., 03h));
              o   the Sequence Indicator (SEQIND) field in the Management Operation Specific field set to
                  01b; and
              o   the identifier whose state is being set,
          to specify to the controller that the command is the first of a sequence of Migration Send commands
          of state data being transferred.
    •     The host may submit Migration Send commands with:
              o   the Select field set to that same management operation;
              o   the SEQIND field cleared to 00b; and
              o   that same identifier whose state is being set,
          to specify to the controller that the command is not the last of the sequence of Migration Send
          commands of state data being transferred, if any.
    •     The host is required to wait for the completion queue entries to be posted for the previous submitted
          Migration Send commands in the sequence of Migration Send commands.
    •     Finally, the host submits the last Migration Send command with:
              o   the Select field set to that same management operation;
              o   the SEQIND field set to 10b; and
              o   that same identifier whose state is being set,




                                                           432
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


         to specify to the controller that this is the last command of the sequence of Migration Send
         commands of the state data being transferred. This last Migration Send command may or may not
         have the Number of Dwords (NUMD) field cleared to 0h.
If a sequence of Migration Send commands of the state data being transferred and the controller processes
a Migration Send command with:
    •    the Select field set to the appropriate management operation (e.g., Set Controller State (i.e., 2h) or
         Set Exported NVM Subsystem State (i.e., 03h));
    •    the Sequence Indicator (SEQIND) field set to 01b; and
    •    the identifier whose state is being set,
then, the command is specifying a new sequence of Migration Send commands of the state data is being
transferred and the previous sequence of Migration Send commands of the state data is discarded.
If a sequence of Migration Send commands of the state data is not being transferred to the specified
controller and the controller processes a Migration Send command with the Sequence Indicator (SEQIND)
field not set to 01b, the controller shall abort that command with a status code of Command Sequence
Error.
If a single Migration Send command is submitted to transfer the entire state data, then the host submits a
Migration Send command with the SEQIND field set to 11b.
          Migration Send Management Operations
5.2.21.2.1 Suspend (Management Operation 0h)
The Suspend management operation of the Migration Send command allows a host to specify the type of
suspend to be done on the specified controller.
The Suspend management operation uses the Command Dword 11 field as defined in Figure 423Figure
423 and does not use the Management Operation Specific field.

                                Figure 423: Suspend – Command Dword 11
 Bits    Description
         Delete User Data Migration Queue (DUDMQ): If this bit is set to ‘1’ and the command completes
         successfully, then the User Data Migration Queue associated with the controller specified in the CNTLID
  31     field, if any, is deleted (refer to the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification). If this bit is
         cleared to ‘0’, then the User Data Migration Queue associated the controller specified in the CNTLID field is
         retained after processing the command, if any.
 30:24   Reserved
         Suspend Type (STYPE): This field specifies the type of suspend.
             Value     Definition
                       Suspend Notification: The specified controller is going to be suspended in the future with
 23:16        0h       a subsequent Migration Send command specifying a Suspend management operation and
                       a non-zero value in the Suspend Type field.
              1h       Suspend: Suspend the controller specified in the CNTLID field as defined in this section.
          All Others Reserved
         Controller Identifier (CNTLID): This field specifies the identifier of the controller to which the Suspend
 15:00
         management operation is performed.

A Suspend Type field value of 0h (i.e., Suspend Notification) allows a host to notify a controller that the
controller specified by the Controller Identifier field is going to be requested to suspend with a subsequent
Migration Send command specifying a Suspend management operation and a non-zero value in the
Suspend Type field.




                                                             433
                                                             NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


A Suspend Type field value of 1h (i.e., Suspend) specifies that the controller specified in the Controller
Identifier field (refer to Figure 423Figure 423) is to be suspended. That controller shall perform the following
actions and then stop initiating transport transactions:
      1. Stop fetching commands until the specified controller is no longer suspended (refer to section
         8.1.14).
      2. Complete the processing of all previously fetched commands, if any, except any outstanding
         Asynchronous Event Request commands.
If:
      •   the command causes the specified controller to be suspended; and
      •   there is a User Data Migration Queue associated with that specified controller,
then:
      •   If the DUDMQ bit is set to ‘1’, then the controller processing the command before posting the
          completion queue entry to the command shall delete that User Data Migration Queue; and
      •   after the specified controller completes the processing of all previously fetched commands, if any,
          except any outstanding Asynchronous Event Request commands, the controller processing the
          Migration Send command shall, at a vendor specific amount of time, posts an entry in that User
          Data Migration Queue that indicates the specified controller is suspended as specified by the
          applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification.
It is not an error if a suspend operation occurs on a controller that is already suspended with the same
Suspend Type value.
If there are not enough free completion queue entries to post the completions of the previously fetched
commands, then the controller may abort the Migration Send command with a status code of Not Enough
Resources.
It is not an error if a suspend operation occurs on a controller that is already suspended with the same
Suspend Type.
If the result of this command causes the specified controller to be suspended, then the specified controller
remains suspended until:
      •   a Migration Send command specifying the Resume management operation (refer to section
          5.2.21.2.2) on the specified controller is completed successfully; or
      •   a Controller Level Reset occurs on the controller processing this command.
If a controller is suspended, then:
      •   accesses to controller properties for that suspended controller shall behave normally except a host
          modification of the CC property that sets CC.EN bit from ‘0’ to ‘1’ (i.e., enabling that suspended
          controller) has implementation specific behavior (i.e., the suspended controller may or may not set
          the CSTS.RDY bit). A host should avoid modifications to controller properties, CMB, and PMR to a
          controller that is suspended;
      •   the Controller Memory Buffer (CMB), if supported, shall behave as defined in section 8.2.1 (i.e.,
          CMB on a suspended controller continues to function normally); and
      •   the Persistent Memory Region (PMR), if supported, shall behave as defined in section 8.2.5 (i.e.,
          PMR on a suspended controller continues to function normally).
5.2.21.2.2 Resume (Management Operation 1h)
The Resume management operation of the Migration Send command is a request for the controller
processing the command to resume the operation of a different controller that is suspended (refer to section
5.2.21.2.1).




                                                      434
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


The Resume management operation uses the Command Dword 11 field as defined in Figure 424Figure
424 and does not use the Management Operation Specific field.

                                 Figure 424: Resume – Command Dword 11
   Bits    Description
  31:16    Reserved
  15:00    Controller Identifier (CNTLID): This field specifies the identifier of the controller to resume operations.

The Resume management operation shall cause the controller specified by the Controller Identifier field
(refer to Figure 424Figure 424) to start fetching and processing commands.
If the specified controller is not suspended (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1), then the controller shall abort the
command with a status code of Controller Not Suspended.
If the controller processing the command has received controller state for the specified controller to be
resumed and that controller state has not been verified and committed (refer to section 5.2.21.2.3), then
the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Command Sequence Error.
5.2.21.2.3 Set Controller State (Management Operation 2h)
The Set Controller State management operation of the Migration Send command allows the host to set the
state of the controller specified by the Controller Identifier (CNTLID) field in the Command Dword 11 field
(refer to Figure 427Figure 427).
The data buffer contains the Controller State data structure specified in Figure 431Figure 431 which
specifies the state to be set in the specified controller.
To set the controller state of the specified controller, the specified controller is required to be in one or more
of these conditions:
     •    Suspended (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1);
     •    enabled (i.e., CC.EN bit is set to ‘1’); or
     •    offline, if that specified controller is a secondary controller.
If the specified controller is not in one of these conditions, then the controller processing the command shall
abort the command with a status code of Invalid Controller Identifier.
The host uses the method defined in section 5.2.21.1 to transfer the controller state where the management
operation is Set Controller State and the controller whose state is being set is the controller specified in the
Controller Identifier field.

5.2.21.2.4 Set Exported NVM Subsystem State (Management Operation 3h)
The Set Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation of the Migration Send command allows
the host to set the state of the Exported NVM Subsystem specified by the Exported NVM Subsystem
Identifier (ESUBID) field in the Command Dword 11 field (refer to Figure 437Figure 437). The data
contained in the data buffer is the Exported NVM Subsystem state data associated with the Exported NVM
Subsystem Template specified by the Exported NVM Subsystem Template Index field in Command Dword
11 field as defined by Figure 437Figure 437.
If the UUID value for the Exported NVM Subsystem Template that was specified when the Exported NVM
Subsystem was created, is not the same as the UUID value for the Exported NVM Subsystem Template
specified by the index in the Exported NVM Subsystem Template Index (ENSTI) field, then the controller
shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command.
To set the Exported NVM Subsystem state of the specified Exported NVM Subsystem, the Underlying
Controllers associated with the specified Exported NVM Subsystem are required to be in one or more of
these conditions:
    •    suspended (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1);
    •    enabled (i.e., CC.EN bit is set to ‘1’); or
    •    offline, if that specified controller is a secondary controller.
If any of the Underlying Controllers in the specified Exported NVM Subsystem are not in one of these
conditions, then the controller processing the command shall abort the command with a status code of
Invalid Field in Command.
The host uses the method defined in section 5.2.21.1 to transfer the Exported NVM Subsystem state where
the management operation is the Set Exported NVM Subsystem State and the identifier whose state is
being set if the Exported NVM Subsystem specified in the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier field
Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier field.

5.2.24 Namespace Attachment command
The Namespace Attachment command is used to attach the specified namespace to controllers or detach
the specified namespace from controllers. The attach and detach operations (refer to section 8.1.17) are
persistent across all reset events. Namespace attach and detach operations are persistent across
Virtualization Management commands that set a secondary controller offline.
The Namespace Attachment command uses the Data Pointer and Command Dword 10 fields. All other
command specific fields are reserved.
The Select field determines the data structure used as part of the command. The data structure is 4,096
bytes in size. The data structure used for Controller Attach and Controller Detach is a Controller List (refer
to section 4.6.1). The controllers to which the specified namespace is to be attached or detached,
respectively, are described in the data structure.
If the SEL field specifies the Controller Attach value, then:
    •      If the Maximum Domain Namespace Attachments (MAXDNA) field in the Identify Controller data
           structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338) is non-zero, then:
               o     For each controller specified in the controller list, if attaching the namespace to that I/O
                     controller causes the sum of the number of namespaces attached to each I/O controller in
                     the Domain to be greater than the value indicated in the MAXDNA field, then the controller
                     shall abort the command with a status code of Namespace Attachment Limit Exceeded;
        and
    •      For each I/O controller specified in the controller list, if the Maximum I/O Controller Namespace
           Attachments (MAXCNA) field in the Identify Controller data structure for that controller is non-zero,
           then:
               o     If attaching the namespace to that I/O controller causes that I/O controller to have the
                     number of attached namespaces to be greater than the value indicated in the MAXCNA
                     field, then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Namespace
                     Attachment Limit Exceeded.
If an attempt is made to attach a namespace to a controller that does not support the corresponding I/O
Command Set, then the command shall be aborted with a status code of I/O Command Set Not Supported.
If an attempt is made to attach a namespace to a controller that supports the corresponding I/O Command
Set and the corresponding I/O Command Set is not enabled by the I/O Command Set profile feature, then
the command shall be aborted with a status code of I/O Command Set Not Enabled.
If a controller in an Underlying NVM Subsystem processes the command and an entry in the Controller List
specifies a controller identifier for an Underlying Controller that is associated with an Exported Controller in
an Exported NVM Subsystem, then:



                                                              444
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •      if the specified Underlying Namespace is associated with an Exported Namespace in that Exported
           NVM Subsystem, then that Exported Namespace shall be attached to the corresponding Exported
           Controller in that Exported NVM Subsystem.
    •      if the specified Underlying Namespace is not associated with an Exported Namespace in that
           Exported NVM Subsystem, then the controller processing the command shall abort that command
           with a status code of Invalid Namespace or Format.

5.2.25 Namespace Management command
The Namespace Management command is used to manage namespaces (refer to section 8.1.17), including
create, delete, and restore namespace configuration operations.
Note: The controller continues to execute commands submitted to I/O Submission Queues while this
operation is in progress.
If the Namespace Management command is supported, then the Namespace Attachment command (refer
to section 5.2.24) shall also be supported. The Namespace Management command shall not be supported
by controllers in an Exported NVM subsystem.
An Underlying Namespace is only able to be deleted if there is no Exported Namespace associated with
that Underlying Namespace. For a delete namespace operation, if the specified namespace is an
Underlying Namespace that is associated with an Exported Namespace, then the controller shall abort the
command with a status code of Command Sequence Error.
The host uses the Namespace Attachment command to attach or detach a namespace to or from a
controller. The create operation does not attach the namespace to a controller. As a side effect of the delete
operation, the namespace is detached from all controllers as the namespace is no longer present in the
system. It is recommended that the host detach all controllers from a namespace prior to deleting the
namespace. If the namespace is not detached from all controllers prior to being deleted, then Attached
Namespace Attribute Changed asynchronous events are reported as specified in section 8.1.17.2. If a
namespace is deleted, then Allocated Namespace Attribute Changed asynchronous events are reported
as specified in section 8.1.17.2.
The data structure used for the create operation is defined in Figure 448Figure 448 and the CSI field
specifies the I/O Command Set. There is no data structure transferred for:
    •      the delete operation; or
    •      the restore default namespace configuration operation (refer to section 5.2.25.1).
The Namespace Management command uses the Data Pointer, Command Dword 10, and Command
Dword 11 fields. All other command specific fields are reserved.
The Namespace Identifier (NSID) field is used as follows for create and delete operations:
    •     Create: The NSID field is reserved for this operation; a host clears this field to a value of 0h. The
          controller shall select an available Namespace Identifier to use for the operation; or
    •     Delete: This field specifies the previously created namespace to delete in this operation. Specifying
          a value of FFFFFFFFh is used to delete all namespaces in the NVM subsystem. If the value of
          FFFFFFFFh is specified and there are zero valid namespaces, the command completes
          successfully.
For the restore default namespace configuration operation, the NSID field:
    •     is not used and should be cleared to a value of 0h; and
    •     shall be ignored by the controller.

           Restore Default Namespace Configuration Operation
The Restore Default Namespace Configuration operation allows a host to restore NVM subsystem
namespace configuration for the current active firmware image. Support for this operation is indicated by
the Restore Default Namespace Configuration Supported (RDNCS) bit (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
The default namespace configuration is defined by the current active firmware image and shall include at
least the number of allocated namespaces, namespace size, and format that are dependent on the specific
I/O Command Sets supported by the controller (refer to the Command Sets Supported (CSS) field in Figure
36Figure 36).
If a controller successfully processes a Namespace Management command that specifies the Restore
Default Namespace Configuration operation, then, prior to the successful completion of the Namespace
Management command, that controller shall:
    •     restore the default namespace configuration; and
    •     set the Default Namespace Configuration Status (DNCS) bit to ‘1’ (refer to Figure 304Figure 304).
If a host submits any command to any controller in the NVM subsystem that results in a change to the
default namespace configuration (refer to section 8.1.17), then the controller shall clear the DNCS bit to ‘0’.
The host is required to delete all namespaces associated with the NVM subsystem before being able to
restore the default namespace configuration using the Restore Default Namespace Configuration
operation.
If a host submits a Namespace Management command that specifies the Restore Default Namespace
Configuration operation and a namespace exists in the NVM subsystem, then the controller shall abort the
command with a status code of Command Sequence Error.
If the controller processes a Namespace Management command that specifies the Restore Default
Namespace Configuration operation and that controller is not able to restore the namespace configuration,
then that controller shall abort the command with a status code of Failed to Restore Configuration.

                                                                NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4

5.2.26 Sanitize command
The Sanitize command is used to start an NVM subsystem sanitize operation (refer to section 1.5.71) or to
recover from a previously failed NVM subsystem sanitize operation. The NVM subsystem sanitize operation
types that may be supported are Block Erase, Crypto Erase, and Overwrite.
An NVM subsystem sanitize operation consists of:
    •     sanitize processing (refer to section 8.1.27), which may include:
              o     deallocation of all media in the NVM subsystem that is allocated for user data; and
              o     additional media modification;
    •     optional verification of media in the NVM subsystem that is allocated for user data; and




                                                         448
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   post-verification deallocation of all media in the NVM subsystem that is allocated for user data
        following media verification, if any, as described in section 8.1.27.
Refer to section 8.1.27.1 for command processing requirements that are common to the Sanitize command
and the Sanitize Namespace command.
The Sanitize command shall not be supported by Exported NVM Subsystems (refer to section 8.1.27.6).
The Sanitize Capabilities (SANICAP) field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure
338) indicates:
    a) the NVM subsystem sanitize operation types supported for the Sanitize command;
    b) whether setting the No-Deallocate After Sanitize (NDAS) bit (refer to Figure 451Figure 451) causes
       media to be modified as part of sanitize processing;
    c) whether the controller inhibits the functionality of the No-Deallocation After Sanitize bit in the
       Sanitize command; and
    d) whether the controller supports the Media Verification state and the Post-Verification Deallocation
       state (refer to the Verification Support (VERS) bit in the SANICAP field in Figure 338Figure 338).
If the Verification Support (VERS) bit is cleared to ‘0’ and a Sanitize command specifies the Enter Media
Verification State (EMVS) bit set to ‘1’ (refer to Figure 451Figure 451), then the controller shall abort the
command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command.
If the Verification Support (VERS) bit is set to ‘1’ and a Sanitize command is processed that specifies:
    a) the Enter Media Verification State (EMVS) bit set to ‘1’, the SANACT field set to a value of 010b
       (i.e., Block Erase) or a value of 100b (i.e., Crypto Erase), and the No-Deallocate After Sanitize
       (NDAS) bit cleared to ‘0’, then successful sanitize processing is followed by entry to the Media
       Verification state;
    b) the Enter Media Verification State (EMVS) bit set to ‘1’ and:
        a) the SANACT field set to 011b (i.e., Overwrite); or
        b) the No-Deallocate After Sanitize (NDAS) bit set to ‘1’,
       then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command;
    c) the SANACT field set to 101b (i.e., Exit Media Verification State) and the sanitization target is in
       the Media Verification state, then:
        •    the controller does not start a new NVM subsystem sanitize operation; and
        •    the sanitization target transitions from the Media Verification state to the Post-Verification
             Deallocation state, in which all media allocated for user data in the NVM subsystem is
             deallocated;
        or
    d) the SANACT field set to 101b (i.e., Exit Media Verification State) and the sanitization target is not
       in the Media Verification state, then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of
       Invalid Field in Command.
If any Persistent Memory Region is enabled in an NVM subsystem, then the controller shall abort any
Sanitize command with a status code of Sanitize Prohibited While Persistent Memory Region is Enabled.
If any namespace is write protected in an NVM subsystem (refer to section 8.1.18), then the controller
aborts any Sanitize command with a status code of Namespace is Write Protected.
If one or more controllers in the NVM subsystem is suspended (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1), then the
controller shall abort the command with a status code of Controller Suspended.
Support for Sanitize commands in a Controller Memory Buffer (i.e., submitted to an Admin Submission
Queue in a Controller Memory Buffer or specifying an Admin Completion Queue in a Controller Memory
Buffer) is implementation specific. If an implementation does not support Sanitize commands in a Controller
Memory Buffer and a controller’s Admin Submission Queue or Admin Completion Queue is in the Controller




                                                         449
                                                                      NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


Memory Buffer, then the controller shall abort all Sanitize commands with a status code of Command Not
Supported for Queue in CMB.
If, at the time the Sanitize command is processed, the controller is able to determine that the sanitize
operation will fail (e.g., the PREQ bit is set to ‘1’, the SANACT field is set to 010b (i.e., Block Erase), and
media containing user data cannot be erased), then the controller should not abort the command because
of that expected failure and the controller should instead report failure of that sanitize operation using the
Sanitize Status log page.
The Sanitize command uses Command Dword 10 and Command Dword 11. All other command specific
fields are reserved.

5.2.27 Sanitize Namespace command
The Sanitize Namespace command is used to start a namespace sanitize operation (refer to section 1.5.66)
or to recover from a previously failed namespace sanitize operation. The only namespace sanitize operation
type is Crypto Erase.
A namespace sanitize operation consists of:
    •   sanitize processing, (refer to section 8.1.27), which may include deallocation of all media that is
        allocated for user data in that namespace;
    •   optional verification of media in the namespace that is allocated for user data; and
    •   post-verification deallocation of all media in the namespace that is allocated for user data following
        media verification, if any, as described in section 8.1.27.
Refer to section 8.1.27.1 for command processing requirements that are common to the Sanitize command
and the Sanitize Namespace command.
The Sanitize Capabilities (SANICAP) field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure
338) indicates:
    a) the namespace sanitize operation types supported for the Sanitize Namespace command; and
    b) whether the controller supports the Media Verification state and the Post-Verification Deallocation
       state (refer to the Namespace Verification Support (NVERS) bit in the SANICAP field in Figure
       338Figure 338).
The Maximum Namespace Sanitize Operations In Progress (MNSOIP) field in the Sanitize Status log page
(refer to Figure 312Figure 312) is used to indicate the maximum number of namespace sanitize operations
that are allowed to be in progress concurrently in the NVM subsystem. If the controller processes a Sanitize
Namespace command that requests the controller to exceed the limit indicated in the MNSOIP field, then
the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Request Exceeds Maximum Namespace
Sanitize Operations In Progress.
If the NSID field:
    •   is cleared to 0h;
    •   is set to FFFFFFFFh;
    •   specifies an inactive NSID; or
    •   specifies a namespace that is in the process of being deleted,
then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Namespace or Format.
If the NVM subsystem is in the Restricted Failure State or is in the Unrestricted Failure state, then the
controller shall abort the command with a status code of Sanitize Failed.
If the Namespace Verification Support (NVERS) bit is set to ‘1’ and a Sanitize Namespace command
specifies:
    a) the Enter Media Verification State (EMVS) bit set to ‘1’, and the SANACT field set to a value of
       100b (i.e., Crypto Erase), then successful sanitize processing is followed by entry to the Media
       Verification state;
    b) the SANACT field set to 101b (i.e., Exit Media Verification State) and the namespace is in the Media
       Verification state, then:
             •   the controller does not start a new namespace sanitize operation; and
             •   the namespace transitions from the Media Verification state to the Post-Verification
                 Deallocation state, in which all media that is allocated for user data in the namespace is
                 deallocated;
        or
    c) the SANACT field set to 101b (i.e., Exit Media Verification State) and the namespace is not in the
       Media Verification state, then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid
       Field in Command.


                                                     452
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If the namespace is write protected (refer to section 8.1.18), then the controller shall abort the Sanitize
Namespace command with a status code of Namespace is Write Protected.
If, at the time the Sanitize Namespace command is processed, the controller is able to determine that the
sanitize operation will fail (e.g., the PREQ bit is set to ‘1’ and a media encryption key for the specified
namespace cannot be changed), then the controller should not abort the command because of that
expected failure and the controller should instead report failure of that sanitize operation using the Sanitize
Status log page.
The Sanitize Namespace command uses Command Dword 10. All other command specific fields are
reserved.

5.2.28 Security Receive command
The Security Receive command transfers the status and data result of one or more Security Send
commands that were previously submitted to the controller.
The association between a Security Receive command and previous Security Send commands is
dependent on the Security Protocol. The format of the data to be transferred is dependent on the Security
Protocol. Refer to SPC-5 for Security Protocol details.
Each Security Receive command returns the appropriate data corresponding to a Security Send command
as defined by the rules of the Security Protocol. The Security Receive command data may not be retained
if there is a loss of communication between the controller and host, or if a Controller Level Reset occurs.
If the Configurable Device Personality feature is supported (refer to section 5.2.30.1.25) and the Security
Personality is supported (refer to section 5.2.13.1.28), then the Security Receive command may have
additional command processing considerations as described in section 5.2.30.1.25.3.
The fields used are Data Pointer, Command Dword 10, and Command Dword 11 fields. All other command
specific fields are reserved.

            of this field.

  31:24     shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command if an unsupported value of the
            Security Protocol is specified.
            SP Specific 1 (SPSP1): The value of this field contains bits 15:08 of the Security Protocol Specific field

5.2.29 Security Send command
The Security Send command is used to transfer security protocol data to the controller. The data structure
transferred to the controller as part of this command contains security protocol specific commands to be
performed by the controller. The data structure transferred may also contain data or parameters associated
with the security protocol commands. Status and data that is to be returned to the host for the security
protocol commands submitted by a Security Send command are retrieved with the Security Receive
command defined in section 5.2.27.
The association between a Security Send command and subsequent Security Receive command is
Security Protocol field dependent as defined in SPC-5.
If the Configurable Device Personality feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.25) is supported and the Security
Personality is supported (refer to section 5.2.13.1.28), then the Security Send command may have
additional command processing considerations as described in section 5.2.30.1.25.3.

           Common Feature Specific Information
Refer to section 3.1.3.6 for mandatory, optional, and prohibited features for the various controller types.
Some Features utilize a data buffer to configure or return attributes for a Feature, whereas others only
utilize a dword in the command or completion queue entry. For more information on Features, including
default value definitions, saved value definitions, and current value definitions, refer to section 4.4.
Upon completion of a Set Features command for a feature, the host should rediscover, re-enumerate and/or
re-initialize all capabilities associated with that feature. For example, if a namespace capability change may
occur for a feature, then the host should pause the use of any associated namespace, submit the Set
Features command for that feature and wait for that command to complete, and then re-issue commands
to all namespaces affected by that Set Features command.
There may be commands in execution when a Feature is changed. The new settings may or may not apply
to commands already submitted for execution when the Feature is changed. Any commands submitted to
a Submission Queue after a Set Features command is successfully completed shall utilize the new settings
for the associated Feature. To ensure that a Features values apply to all subsequent commands, the host
should allow commands being processed to complete prior to issuing the Set Features command.




                                                                  459
                                                               NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If the controller does not support a changeable value for a Feature (i.e., the Feature is not changeable,
refer to section 5.2.12.2), and a Set Features command for that Feature is processed, then if that command
specifies a Feature value that:
    •     is not the same as the existing value for that Feature, then the controller shall abort that command
          with a status code of Feature Not Changeable; and
    •     is the same as the existing value for that Feature, then the controller may:
              o     complete that command successfully; or
              o     abort that command with a status code of Feature Not Changeable.
Refer to each feature description in this section for any additional requirements associated with that feature.
5.2.30.1.1        Arbitration (Feature Identifier 01h)
This Feature controls command arbitration within the controller. Refer to section 3.4.4 for command
arbitration details. The attributes are specified in Command Dword 11.
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then the attributes specified in Figure 467Figure 467 are returned in Dword 0
of the completion queue entry for that command.

5.2.30.1.2        Power Management (Feature Identifier 02h)
This Feature allows the host to configure the controller power state. The attributes are specified in
Command Dword 11 (refer to Figure 468Figure 468).
Upon successful completion of a Set Features command for this Feature, the controller shall be in the
Power State specified. For a transition to a non-operational power state, the device may exceed the power
indicated for that non-operational power state as defined in section 8.1.19.1 (e.g., while completing this
command). If enabled, autonomous power state transitions continue to occur from the new state.
The default value of the Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit (IIELL) attribute of the Power Management feature shall
be the value in the Minimum Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit (MIIELL) field in the Power State 0 Descriptor (PSD0)
field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
If a Get Features command with the SEL field not set to 011b completes successfully for this Feature, then
the attributes described in Figure 469Figure 469 are returned in Dword 0 of the completion queue entry for
that command.

              Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit Attribute
An Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit is the maximum additional response latency for the next I/O command
performed by an idle controller as compared to a non-idle controller. A non-zero value in the Idle I/O Exit
Latency Limit Support and Scope (IIELLSS) field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure
338Figure 338) indicates that Idle I/O Exit Latency Limits are supported and that value indicates whether
there is an Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit for each operational power state or a single Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit
for all operational power states.
The Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit is the maximum latency from when the I/O command is submitted (e.g., I/O
Submission Queue Tail Doorbell is written) to an idle controller until that controller is able to:
    a) process and complete I/O commands; and
    b) access the resources (e.g., formatted storage) associated with attached namespace(s), if any, as
       part of I/O command processing.
If the additional response latency depends on the specific I/O command or fields in an I/O command (e.g.,
the size of an I/O command), then the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification specifies
the command whose additional response latency is used to specify an Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit for that
I/O Command Set. Other I/O commands may exceed that limit.
If Idle I/O Exit Latency Limits are supported, then upon successful completion of a Set Features command
for this Feature that specifies a non-zero Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit for an operational power state, the
controller shall not exceed the specified Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit for the next I/O command the controller
was idle (i.e., transitioned from idle to non-idle to process that I/O command) and in the power state
specified by that Set Features command.
If the IIELLSS field indicates Global scope (i.e., that field is set to 10b), then the controller shall not exceed
the specified Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit for the next I/O command while the controller was idle (i.e.,
transitioned from idle to non-idle to process that I/O command) and in any operational power states.


                                                                461
                                                                 NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If a Set Features command specifies:
    •     an operational power state;
    •     the IIELLSS field is set to 01b; and
    •     the value in the IIELL field (refer to Figure 468Figure 468) is both greater than 0h and less than the
          value indicated in the Minimum Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit (MIIELL) field in the Power State
          Descriptor data structure (refer to Figure 340Figure 340) for the power state specified in the Power
          State (PS) field,
then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command.
If a Set Features command specifies:
    •     an operational power state;
    •     the IIELLSS field is set to 10b; and
    •     the value in the IIELL field is both greater than 0h and less than the minimum idle I/O exit latency
          limit value the controller is able to support,
then the controller shall use that minimum value to process the command instead of the value specified in
the IIELL field. The host is able to observe the resulting Idle I/O Exit Latency Limit value by submitting a
Get Features command (refer to Figure 469Figure 469) with the Select field not set to 11b for this Feature.

5.2.30.1.3      Temperature Threshold (Feature Identifier 04h)
This Feature allows the host to configure temperature thresholds. The attributes are specified in Command
Dword 11 (refer to Figure 470Figure 470).
A controller may report up to nine temperature values in the SMART / Health Information log page (i.e., the
Composite Temperature and Temperature Sensor 1 through Temperature Sensor 8; refer to Figure
213Figure 213). Associated with each implemented temperature sensor is an over temperature threshold
and an under temperature threshold. When a temperature is greater than or equal to its corresponding over
temperature threshold or less than or equal to its corresponding under temperature threshold, then the
Temperature Threshold Condition (TTC) bit is set to ‘1’ in the Critical Warning field in the SMART / Health
Information log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.3). This may trigger an asynchronous event.
The over temperature threshold feature shall be implemented for Composite Temperature. The under
temperature threshold Feature shall be implemented for Composite Temperature if a non-zero Warning
Composite Temperature Threshold (WCTEMP) field value is reported in the Identify Controller data
structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338). The over temperature threshold and under temperature threshold
features shall be implemented for all implemented temperature sensors (i.e., all Temperature Sensor fields
that report a non-zero value).
The default value of the over temperature threshold feature for Composite Temperature is the value in the
WCTEMP field in the Identify Controller data structure if the value of the WCTEMP field is non-zero;
otherwise, the default value is implementation specific. The default value of the under temperature threshold
feature for Composite Temperature is implementation specific. The default value of the over temperature
threshold for all implemented temperature sensors is FFFFh. The default value of the under temperature
threshold for all implemented temperature sensors is 0h.




                                                         462
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then the temperature threshold selected by Command Dword 11 is returned
in Dword 0 of the completion queue entry for that command.
              Temperature Threshold Hysteresis
This functionality allows the host to specify the temperature hysteresis that a controller shall use to
determine the end of a temperature threshold event.
If the controller supports the use of the Temperature Threshold Hysteresis feature as indicated by at non-
zero value of the TMPTHMH field (refer to Figure 338Figure 338), then the controller shall:
    •     support this feature for the Composite Temperature value (refer to Figure 470Figure 470); and
    •     support the Temperature Threshold Hysteresis Recovery event (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
If hysteresis is supported for Threshold Temperature Select values other than Composite Temperature (i.e.,
0h) (refer to Figure 470Figure 470); then, associated with each implemented temperature sensor is an over-
temperature threshold and an under-temperature threshold with a hysteresis value. If the host specifies
hysteresis for a Threshold Temperature Select that is not supported, the controller shall abort the command
with a status of Invalid Field in Command.
An over-temperature threshold hysteresis event begins when the value of a temperature field (refer to the
temperature values reported as described in section 5.2.30.1.3) transitions from less than its corresponding
temperature threshold to greater than or equal to that temperature threshold. That over-temperature
threshold hysteresis event ends when the value of that temperature field transitions from greater than or
equal to that temperature threshold to less than that temperature threshold minus the value of the
Temperature Threshold Hysteresis (TMPTHH) field.
An under-temperature threshold hysteresis event begins when the value of a temperature field transitions
from greater than its corresponding temperature threshold to less than or equal to that temperature
threshold. That under-temperature threshold hysteresis event ends when the value of that temperature field
transitions from less than or equal to that temperature threshold to greater than that temperature threshold
plus the value of the Temperature Threshold Hysteresis (TMPTHH) field.
When a temperature threshold hysteresis event has started, the Temperature Threshold Condition (TTC)
is set to ‘1’ in the Critical Warning field in the SMART / Health Information log page (refer to section
5.2.13.1.3) is set to ‘1’. This may trigger an initial asynchronous event.
At the end of a temperature threshold hysteresis event, a Temperature Threshold Hysteresis Recovery
event shall be triggered (refer to Figure 474Figure 474), the TTC bit (refer to section 5.2.13.1.3) shall be
cleared to ’0’ and the Warning Composite Temperature Time field shall stop accumulating the number of
minutes.
If the value of the Temperature Threshold Hysteresis field is larger than the value supported by the controller
as indicated by the TMPTHMH field in Figure 338Figure 338, the controller shall abort the command with a
status code of Invalid Field in Command.

  24:22      not apply.

5.2.30.1.4      Volatile Write Cache (Feature Identifier 06h)
This Feature controls the volatile write cache, if present, on the controller. If a volatile write cache is present
(refer to the VWC field in Figure 338Figure 338), then this Feature shall be supported. The attributes are
specified in Command Dword 11.
Note: If the controller is able to guarantee that data present in a write cache is written to non-volatile storage
media on loss of power, then that write cache is considered non-volatile and this Feature does not apply to
that write cache.
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then the attributes specified in Figure 471Figure 471 are returned in Dword 0
of the completion queue entry for that command.
If a volatile write cache is not present, then:
    •     if a Set Features command specifies the Volatile Write Cache feature identifier, then the controller
          shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command; and
    •     if a Get Features command specifies the Volatile Write Cache feature identifier, then the controller
          shall abort the command with a status code of Invalid Field in Command.
If a volatile write cache is present and the volatile write cache is disabled (i.e., the WCE bit is cleared to
‘0’), then the user data written by any command to a namespace shall be persistent. Refer to the Volatile
Write Cache Not Present field contained in the Common Namespace Features field in Figure 346Figure
346.

5.2.30.1.5        Number of Queues (Feature Identifier 07h)
This Feature allocates I/O queues for the controller processing the command. The host should only submit
a Set Features command for this Feature during initialization prior to creation of any I/O Submission and/or
I/O Completion Queues. If a Set Features command is submitted for this Feature after creation of any I/O
Submission and/or I/O Completion Queues, then the controller shall abort that Set Features command with
status code of Command Sequence Error. For a Set Features command, the attributes are specified in
Command Dword 11 (refer to Figure 472Figure 472). For a Get Features command, Command Dword 11
is ignored by the controller.
If a:
        •    Set Features command completes successfully for this Feature; or
        •    Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities)
             completes successfully for this Feature,
then the number of I/O queues allocated by the controller are returned in Dword 0 of the completion queue
entry for that command (refer to Figure 473Figure 473).
After a Controller Level Reset (CLR), the first Set Features command for this Feature that the controller
completes successfully shall allocate I/O queues for that controller.
After that first successful Set Features command, the number of I/O queues allocated for the controller shall
not change until a CLR occurs on the controller.
If the host submits a Set Features command for this Feature:
        •    after that first successful Set Features command;
        •    before subsequent creation of any I/O Submission and/or I/O Completion Queues; and
        •    before any subsequent CLR,
then the controller should complete that Set Features command successfully without changing the number
of allocated I/O queues.

5.2.30.1.6     Asynchronous Event Configuration (Feature Identifier 0Bh)

successfully for this Feature, then the attributes specified in Figure 474Figure 474 are returned in Dword 0

5.2.30.1.8     Timestamp (Feature Identifier 0Eh)
This Feature enables the host to set a timestamp value in the controller. A controller indicates support for
the Timestamp feature through the Optional NVM Command Support (ONCS) field in the Identify Controller
data structure. The Timestamp field value (refer to Figure 479Figure 479) in a Set Features command sets
a timestamp value in the controller. After the current value for this Feature is set, the controller updates that
value as time passes. A Get Features command that requests the current value reports the timestamp
value in the controller at the time the Get Features command is processed (e.g., the value set with a Set
Features command for the current value plus the elapsed time since being set).
Note: If the Timestamp feature is saveable (refer to Figure 201) and the host saves a value, then the
timestamp value restored after a subsequent power on or reset event is the value that was saved (refer to
section 4.4). As a result, the timestamp may appear to move backwards in time.




                                                               469
                                                                      NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


The accuracy of a Timestamp value after initialization may be affected by vendor specific factors, such as
whether the controller continuously counts after the timestamp is initialized, or whether the controller stops
counting during certain intervals (e.g., non-operational power states). If the controller stops counting during
such intervals, then the Synch bit in the Timestamp – Data Structure for Get Features (refer to Figure
480Figure 480) shall be set to ‘1’.
For each method of initiating a Controller Level Reset (CLR), if the controller maintains (i.e., continues to
update) the timestamp value across a CLR initiated by that method (e.g., a Controller Reset), then the
controller shall also preserve the Timestamp Origin field (refer to Figure 480Figure 480) across a CLR
initiated by that method.
If the controller does not maintain the value of the timestamp across the most recent Controller Level Reset,
then the Timestamp field is cleared to 0h due to that Controller Level Reset.
Timestamp values should not be used for security applications. Other application use of the Timestamp
feature is outside the scope of this specification.
If a Set Features command is issued for this Feature, the data structure specified in Figure 479Figure 479
is transferred in the data buffer for that command, specifying the Timestamp value.

                            Figure 479: Timestamp – Data Structure for Set Features
  Bytes      Description
             Timestamp (TSTMP): Number of milliseconds that have elapsed since midnight, 01-Jan-1970, UTC. Refer
  05:00
             to ISO 8601 for format requirements.
  07:06      Reserved

successfully for this Feature, then the data structure specified in Figure 480Figure 480 is returned in the

          If the Timestamp Origin field cleared to 000b, then this field is set to the time in milliseconds since the last
          Controller Level Reset.

05:00     If the Timestamp Origin field is set to 001b, then this field is set to the last Timestamp value set by the host, plus
          the time in milliseconds since the Timestamp was set. If the sum of the Timestamp value set by the host and the

          If the Synch bit is set to ‘1’, then the Timestamp value may be reduced by vendor specific time intervals not
          counted by the controller.

5.2.30.1.15     Host Behavior Support (Feature Identifier 16h)
This Feature enables use of controller functionality that is associated with and depends upon specific host
behavior that may or may not be supported by all hosts. A controller does not use such functionality unless
the host has specified that the host supports the specific host behavior upon which the functionality
depends. The host specifies that support to the controller by setting a field in this Feature. That host action
enables controller use of the associated functionality with that host. A controller shall not use functionality
with a host that has not indicated support for the associated specific host behavior upon which that controller
functionality depends. The attributes in Figure 491Figure 491 are transferred in the data buffer.
For example, the Command Interrupted status code is associated with and depends upon the specific host
behavior that the host is expected to retry commands that are aborted with that status code. That command
retry behavior may or may not be supported by all hosts (e.g., hosts compliant with revision 1.3 and earlier
of the NVM Express Base Specification are unlikely to retry commands aborted with the Command
Interrupted status code as that status code was introduced after NVM Express Base Specification, Revision
1.3). A host that supports that command retry behavior specifies that support to the controller by setting a
field to 1h in the Host Behavior Support Feature. Setting that field to 1h enables controller use of the
Command Interrupted status code, with the result that this status code is used only with hosts that have
specified support for the associated command retry behavior.
This Feature is not saveable (refer to Figure 201). The default value of this Feature shall be all bytes cleared
to 0h.
After a successful completion of a Set Features command for this Feature, the controller may use controller-
to-host functionality that depends on specific host behavior as indicated by the attributes. If multiple Set
Features commands for this Feature are processed by the controller, only information from the most recent
successful command is retained (i.e., subsequent commands replace information provided by previous
commands).
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then the attributes specified in Figure 491Figure 491 are returned in the data
buffer for that command.

5.2.30.1.23     Namespace Admin Label (Feature Identifier 1Fh)
The Namespace Admin Label feature provides the ability to set and get the Namespace Admin Label for a
namespace. This Feature shall be saveable and therefore shall not be supported if the Save and Select

Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338). The attributes in Figure 507Figure 507
are transferred in the data buffer.
The saved value and current value of this Feature shall be identical. If the SV bit is cleared to ‘0’ in a Set
Features command that specifies this Feature, the controller shall abort the command with a status code
of Invalid Field in the Command. If the value of the Namespace Admin Label is changed by means outside
the scope of this standard, then that change shall affect the results of any subsequent Get Features
command that specifies this Feature.
The default value of this Feature is all nulls (i.e., all bytes cleared to 0h). Sanitize operations (refer to section
8.1.27) affect the values of this Feature; any successful sanitize operation shall modify this Feature by
resetting both the saved value and the current value to the default value (refer to Figure 770Figure 770).
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then the attributes specified in Figure 507Figure 507 are returned in the data
buffer for that command.

  255:0
              in identifying a namespace (e.g., based on the contents of the data stored in the namespace (e.g., “Q4
              2018 Financial Records”) or the application intended to use the namespace (e.g., “CRM data”)).

5.2.30.1.24     Controller Data Queue (Feature Identifier 21h)
This Feature allows a host to update the status of the head pointer of a Controller Data Queue (CDQ) and
specify the configuration of a Controller Data Queue Tail event. The CDQ is specified by the Controller
Data Queue Identifier (CDQID) field in Command Dword 11 (refer to Figure 508Figure 508).
The Head Pointer field specifies the current slot of the head pointer in the queue (refer to section 8.1.7).
The controller uses this value to determine if CDQ entries have been freed by the host.
If the Enable Tail Pointer Trigger (ETPT) bit is set to ‘1’, then when the slot specified by the Tail Pointer
Trigger (TPT) field for the specified CDQ is posted with an entry, the controller shall generate a Controller
Data Queue Tail Pointer event to the host (refer to section 8.1.7).
If the Set Features command is successful and there is a pending Controller Data Queue Tail Pointer event
for the specified CDQ, then the controller shall clear that pending event.
A controller should report Controller Data Queue Tail Pointer events in the order of occurrence to avoid
reporting the same Controller Data Queue when a Controller Data Queue Tail Pointer event for that
Controller Data Queue is being repeatedly triggered.




                                                             483
                                                                    NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If the Enable Tail Pointer Trigger (ETPT) bit is set to ‘1’ in the current value of this Feature (refer to section
4.4) and the controller processes a Set Features command for this Feature that specifies:
     •    the Enable Tail Pointer Trigger (ETPT) bit set to ‘1’; and
     •    a slot in the Tail Pointer Trigger (TPT) field,
then prior to posting the completion for that Set Features command, the controller may post an entry into
the specified CDQ in the slot specified by the value of the TPT field that had been set prior to processing
that Set Features command. To detect this condition, after receiving the completion of that Set Features
command, a host should examine the CDQ to determine if the requested tail pointer trigger has already
occurred. If the requested tail pointer trigger has occurred, then a subsequent Set Features command
should be submitted by the host to disable the Tail Pointer Trigger event or request a different tail pointer
trigger.
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this Feature, then:
    •     the attributes described in Figure 508Figure 508 are returned in Dword 0 of the completion queue
          entry; and
    •     the attributes described in Figure 511Figure 511 are returned in the data buffer for that command.

                          Figure 508: Controller Data Queue – Command Dword 11

This Feature is not saveable and is persistent (refer to Figure 466Figure 466). The settings for each
personality shall persist across power cycles and resets.
A personality is able to be frozen. If a personality is frozen, then the settings of that personality are not
allowed to be changed. If an authentication method is supported by that personality, as described in section




                                                                    487
                                                            NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


5.2.30.1.25.1, then that frozen personality is able to be unfrozen. If no authentication method is supported
by that personality, then that frozen personality is permanently frozen.
NVM Express does not provide any guidance on whether modifying the NVM subsystem by changing the
settings of a personality affects compliance with any applicable laws, specifications, or other requirements.
                 Authentication Methods
This section defines optional authentication methods that allow a host to unfreeze a previously frozen
personality. Support for these authentication methods is indicated in the Authenticated Unfreeze Support
(AUS) field in the Personality Properties data structure (refer to Figure 292Figure 292). Section 8.1.6.2
describes the mechanisms to unfreeze a frozen personality.
The Security Send and Security Receive commands are used by the host to submit Personality Unfreeze
Request operations (refer to section 8.1.6.2). If the Security Send and Security Receive commands are not
supported, a frozen personality is permanently frozen.
If a personality supports Physical Credential Authentication (refer to the PCAS bit in Figure 292Figure 292),
then the credential is a vendor-defined Physical Presence Indicator (PPI) as described in section
5.2.30.1.25.1.1.
If a personality supports Programmable Key Authentication (refer to the PKAS bit in Figure 292Figure 292),
then the authentication key is derived from a host-programmable key as described in section
5.2.30.1.25.1.2.
5.2.30.1.25.1.1 Physical Credential Authentication
Physical Credential Authentication (refer to the PCAS bit in Figure 292Figure 292) provides the means to
unfreeze a currently frozen personality using a Physical Presence Indicator (PPI).
The physical credential is a vendor-defined PPI that is only readable by someone with physical possession
of the device (e.g., an identifier printed in the device label) and is prohibited to be returned to the host by
any programmatic interface (e.g., a command).
Refer to the TCG Storage Opal SSC Feature Set: PSID Specification for recommended guidelines on how
to implement a physical credential. It is recommended that the length of the authentication credential be 32
bytes minimum.
5.2.30.1.25.1.2 Programmable Key Authentication
Programmable Key Authentication (refer to the PKAS bit in Figure 292Figure 292) provides the means to
unfreeze a currently frozen personality using an HMAC that is calculated using a key that is derived from a
host-programmable key (i.e., Derived HMAC Key (DHK)) as described in section 8.1.6.3.1. The DHK is only
able to be programmed in the NVM subsystem if there is no DHK programmed. If there is a DHK
programmed, then that DHK is able to be purged by submitting a Set Features command that specifies the
Manufacturing Default Personality (refer to section 5.2.30.1.25.2). If a personality supports Programmable
Key Authentication and:
    •   a DHK has not been programmed, then that personality is able to be frozen, but not unfrozen; or
    •   a DHK has been programmed, then that personality is able to be frozen and unfrozen.
Protecting a frozen personality from being unfrozen, unless authenticated by the DHK, is enabled by
programming a DHK. The programming of the DHK (refer to section 8.1.6.3) should be done in a secure
environment (e.g., as part of the manufacturing process).
The DHK is utilized to sign security personality authenticated requests (refer to section 8.1.6.2.2) sent to
the controller using a Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) generated according to the CDP
Authentication Algorithm specified by the host and supported by the controller (refer to the CDPALG field
in Figure 338Figure 338).




                                                     488
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


Use of a random number (i.e., random nonce) provides additional protection against replay of authenticated
requests where authenticated requests are recorded and played back later by an attacker (refer to section
8.1.1.1).
                 Manufacturing Default Personality (Personality Identifier 00h)
The Manufacturing Default Personality contains no settings and allows a host to change the settings of
other personalities to their manufacturing default values (refer to Figure 513Figure 513). This personality is
used to ensure all settings of each affected personality, other than the Revert to Subsystem Manufacturing
Settings Personality, are changed to the manufacturing default values. The Manufacturing Default
Personality changes the current value of the feature for each affected personality to the default value of
that feature and may also change other personality settings outside of the current values of the feature
(e.g., vendor-specific personality settings that are not visible to the host, personality settings that are not
indicated by the feature values but are indicated to the host via some other mechanism such as a field in
the Identify Controller data structure). A personality that is permanently frozen (refer to section 8.1.6.1.2) is
not an affected personality and is indicated by the AUS field being cleared to zero in the Personality
Properties data structure (refer to Figure 292Figure 292) for that personality in the Device Personalities log
page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.28).
Individually setting the current value of the feature for each affected personality, other than the
Manufacturing Default Personality and the Revert to Subsystem Manufacturing Settings Personality, to the
default value of the feature for that personality may or may not change all personality settings to the
manufacturing default values. (i.e., setting the Manufacturing Default Personality may change settings
outside of the current values of the feature for each affected personality).
If a Set Features command that specifies the Configurable Device Personality feature and the
Manufacturing Default Personality completes successfully, then for any subsequent Get Features
command that specifies a personality, other than:
     •   the Manufacturing Default Personality; and
     •   the Revert to Subsystem Manufacturing Settings Personality,
that was affected by that Set Features command, the controller shall set the Personality Manufacturing
Default Settings State (PMDSS) bit to ‘1’ in the completion queue entry for that Get Features command
(refer to Figure 514Figure 514).
If a Set Features command that specifies the Configurable Device Personality feature and the
Manufacturing Default Personality, completes successfully, then for any subsequent Get Features
command that specifies the Manufacturing Default Personality:
    •    If there are no personalities that are permanently frozen other than those that were permanently
         frozen at the time the device was manufactured, if any, then the controller shall set the PMDSS bit
         to ‘1’ in the completion queue entry for that Get Features command; and
    •    If there is any personality that is permanently frozen that was not permanently frozen at the time
         the device was manufactured, then the controller shall clear the PMDSS bit to ‘0’ in the completion
         queue entry for that Get Features command.
If the controller supports the Configurable Device Personality feature, then the Manufacturing Default
Personality is supported by the controller. The Manufacturing Default Personality may be frozen or unfrozen
at the time of manufacturing.
The following conditions are required for the host to be able to change personalities to the manufacturing
default settings using the Manufacturing Default Personality. If any of these conditions are not met, then
the controller shall not change the settings of any personality and shall abort a Set Features command that
requests the Manufacturing Default Personality with a status code of Feature Not Changeable:
    •    the Manufacturing Default personality is not frozen;
    •    each personality that is able to be unfrozen (refer to the AUS field in Figure 292Figure 292) is
         unfrozen (i.e., the PERFS bit is cleared to ‘0’ in a Get Features command for each such personality,
         refer to Figure 514Figure 514); and



                                                          489
                                                             NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   all conditions necessary to change each personality that is able to be unfrozen, as defined for that
        personality, if any, are satisfied (e.g., the Security Personality (refer to section 5.2.30.1.25.3), the
        security protocols (e.g., TCG) have been reset to their default security settings as specified for each
        security protocol (refer to section 5.2.30.1.25.3)).
Some personalities may have an effect on user data when changing configurations as indicated by the
Personality Settings Change User Data Effect (PSCUDE) bit (refer to Figure 292Figure 292).
If the Derived HMAC Key (DHK) is programmed in the NVM subsystem (refer to section 8.1.6.3.1), then
that DHK shall be purged (refer to IEEE Std 2883) as part of the NVM subsystem successfully being
configured with the Manufacturing Default Personality. The DHK shall not be purged by any other operation
(e.g., as part of a sanitize operation or Format NVM command).
                Security Personality (Personality Identifier 01h)
The Security Personality allows a host to configure the NVM subsystem to operate with one or more of the
supported security protocols indicated in Figure 516Figure 516, or to prohibit operation with one or more of
those supported security protocols.
If an NVM subsystem is configured using the Security Personality and a security protocol has been enabled,
then any Security Send and Security Receive command issued by the host that specifies that security
protocol shall be allowed.
If a security protocol is allowed, then once the security protocol is no longer in the defined default
manufacturing state for that security protocol (e.g., upon transition out of the Manufacturing-Inactive state
for the TCG Security Protocol (refer to the TCG Storage Security Subsystem Class: Opal Specification)),
then the controller shall:
    •    freeze the Security Personality; and
    •    record a CDP Change Event in the Persistent Event log page for the Security Personality (refer to
         section 5.2.13.1.14.2.15).
If a security protocol is prohibited, then any Security Send and Security Receive command issued by the
host that specifies that security protocol shall be prohibited. If a Security Send or Security Receive
command is processed that uses a security protocol that is prohibited, then the controller shall abort the
command with a status code of Access Denied.
If a Get Features command with the Select field not set to 011b (i.e., Supported Capabilities) completes
successfully for this personality, then the Security Personality data structure defined in Figure 516Figure
516 shall be returned in the data buffer for that command.

                  Lockdown Persistence Personality (Personality Identifier 02h)
The Lockdown Persistence Personality allows a host to persist the prohibitions specified by the Lockdown
command (refer to section 5.2.13) that affect all controllers in the NVM subsystem across power cycles.
If this personality is supported, then the Lockdown command shall be supported.
If a Set Features command is submitted for this personality, then the attributes described in Figure
518Figure 518 are specified in Command Dword 11 for that command.

                 Figure 518: Lockdown Persistence Personality – Command Dword 11

         Lockdown Persistence Enable (LDPE): If this bit is set to ‘1’, then Lockdown Persistence shall be enabled,
         and the prohibitions of the Lockdown command that affect all controllers in the NVM subsystem shall persist
         across power cycles of the NVM subsystem.
  00
         If this bit is cleared to ‘0’, then Lockdown Persistence shall be disabled, and the prohibitions specified by
         the Lockdown command that affect all controllers in the NVM subsystem shall not persist across power
         cycles of the NVM subsystem.

If a Get Features command specifying this personality is successfully processed, then the attributes
described in Figure 519Figure 519 are returned in Dword 1 of the completion queue entry for that command
and shall indicate the current status of this personality.
