          ANA Considerations
If more than one participating NVM subsystem contains controllers that provide a host with access to a
dispersed namespace, then Asymmetric Namespace Access (ANA) and Asymmetric Namespace Access
Reporting (refer to section 8.1.1) should be supported in all participating NVM subsystems. If ANA is used
with dispersed namespaces, then globally unique namespace identifiers (refer to section 8.1.10.2) are used
to determine when multiple paths are available to the same dispersed namespace. Hosts specify to
controllers that their host (e.g., multipath I/O software) uses globally unique namespace identifiers to
determine when multiple paths are available to the dispersed namespace by setting the HDISNS field to 1h
in the Host Behavior Support feature, as described in section 8.1.10.3.
ANA Group usage with dispersed namespaces is described in section 8.1.1.2.
          Reservation Considerations
Reservations for a dispersed namespace that is able to be accessed by controllers in multiple participating
NVM subsystems are intended to be coordinated between each participating NVM subsystem. To ensure
the uniqueness of a host’s identity and prevent potential data corruption, each host that sets the Host
Dispersed Namespace Support (HDISNS) field to 1h in the Host Behavior Support feature specifies a Host
Identifier that is unique across all hosts that connect to any participating NVM subsystem, as described in
section 8.1.10.3.
If a host is a reservation registrant on a dispersed namespace, and that host submits a Reservation Report
command to that namespace, then for reservations established using controllers that are not contained in
the same participating NVM subsystem as the controller processing the Reservation Report command, the
Controller ID (CNTLID) field shall be set to FFFDh in the Registrant data structure (refer to Figure 673Figure
673) or Registrant Extended data structure (refer to Figure 674Figure 674). Multiple identical Registrant or
Registrant Extended data structures with the CNTLID field set to FFFDh shall not be returned by a single
Reservation Report command; as a result, a Registrant or Registrant Extended data structure with the
CNTLID field set to FFFDh indicates one or more controllers are associated with a host that is a registrant
of the dispersed namespace in another participating NVM subsystem. A Registrant or Registrant Extended
data structure with the CNTLID field set to FFFDh is returned for each host (i.e., as identified by the HOSTID


                                                           633
                                                                       NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


field in that data structure) that is a registrant of the dispersed namespace in any other participating NVM
subsystem.
The Dispersed Namespace Reservation Support (DISNSRS) bit in a command is set to ‘1’ by hosts that
support reservations on dispersed namespaces (i.e., hosts that support receiving a value of FFFDh in the
CNTLID field of a Registrant data structure or Registrant Extended data structure). A controller that supports
dispersed namespaces and supports reservations (i.e., a controller that has the Reservations Support
(RESERVS) bit set to ‘1’ in the Optional NVM Command Support (ONCS) field of the Identify Controller
data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338)) shall support the DISNSRS bit being set to ‘1’ in each
command in the following list:
    •   Reservation Acquire (refer to section 7.5);
    •   Reservation Register (refer to section 7.6);
    •   Reservation Release (refer to section 7.7); and
    •   Reservation Report (refer to section 7.8).
If the HDISNS field is set to 1h in the Host Behavior Support feature and the DISNSRS bit is cleared to ‘0’
in any of the commands in the preceding list when submitted to a dispersed namespace, then the controller
shall abort that command with a status code of Namespace Is Dispersed.

to allow a host, the Administrating Host, to create, configure, and delete Exported NVM Subsystems.

    •   Manage Exported Port command (refer to section 5.4.6),
to allow the Administrating Host to create, configure, and delete Exported NVM Subsystems.

    •   Migration Send command (refer to section 5.2.21) with the Set Exported NVM Subsystem State

to allow the Administrating Host to migrate an Exported NVM Subsystem.
An Exported NVM Subsystem shall not report any information about Underlying NVM Subsystem resources
or entities that is not associated with that Exported NVM Subsystem.
         Common Management of Exported NVM Resources
This section describes operations to an Exported NVM Subsystem that are common to both memory-based
controllers and message-based controllers.
8.1.11.1.1 Creating an Exported NVM Subsystem
To create the Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating Host submits a Manage Exported NVM
Subsystem Receive command (refer to section 5.2.18) specifying:
    •   the Select field set to Create Exported NVM Subsystem (i.e., 0h); and
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Template Index field (refer to Figure 380Figure 380) for the index
        into the Exported NVM Subsystem Template UUID List (refer to section 5.2.14.2.23) that
        corresponds to the UUID for that Exported NVM Subsystem Template, if an Exported NVM
        Template (refer to section 8.1.11.1.3) is specified to be applied to the created Exported NVM
        Subsystem (i.e., the Template Required bit (refer to Figure 380Figure 380) is set to ‘1’).
Additional command settings for message-based controllers are described in section 8.1.11.1.1.1.
The NVM subsystem indicates the maximum number of Exported NVM Subsystems allowed to be created
in the NVM subsystem in the Maximum Number of Exported NVM Subsystems (MNENS) field in the Identify
Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338). If the Administrating Host submits a Manage
Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command to request the creation of a new Exported NVM Subsystem
and the number of Exported NVM Subsystems that exists equals the value in the MNENS field, then the
command is aborted as specified in section 5.2.18.1.1.
On successful completion of the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command:


                                                   636
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   an Exported NVM Subsystem is created;
    •   Dword 0 of the completion queue entry indicates the Exported NVM Subsystem identifier (refer to
        Figure 382Figure 382); and
    •   the data buffer contains the NVMe Qualified Name (NQN) of the Exported NVM Subsystem.
Subsequent commands that specify that created Exported NVM Subsystem define whether the command
uses:
    •   either the Exported NVM Subsystem identifier or the NQN of the Exported NVM Subsystem;
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem identifier; or
    •   the NQN of the Exported NVM Subsystem,
to specify that created Exported NVM Subsystem.
The created Exported NVM Subsystem and any modifications to that Exported NVM Subsystem
configuration remains persistent in the Underlying NVM Subsystem across all Controller Level Resets until
that Exported NVM Subsystem is deleted (refer to section 8.1.11.1.4 and section 8.1.11.1.5 on how to
delete the created Exported NVM Subsystem).
            Message-based Transport Extensions
For Message-based controllers, in the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command that is used
to create an Exported NVM Subsystem, the host sets the Restricted Access (RA) bit (refer to Figure
383Figure 383) to either allow unrestricted host access or restrict access to specific hosts.
After creating an Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating Host is able to optionally assigning access
control policies for the Exported NVM Subsystem (refer to section 5.2.19.1.3 and section 5.2.19.1.4).
8.1.11.1.2 Managing Exported Namespaces
An Administrating Host uses the Manage Exported Namespace command (refer to section 5.2.17) to create
and delete associations between an Underlying Namespace in an Underlying NVM Subsystem to an
Exported Namespace in the specified Exported NVM Subsystem.
An Administrating Host is able to associate an Underlying Namespace to an Exported NVM Subsystem by
submitting a Manage Exported Namespace command specifying:
    •   the Select field set to Associate Namespace (i.e., 01h);
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier in the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier (ESUBID) field
        (refer to Figure 370Figure 370) or the SUBNQN in the Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSNQN)
        field (refer to Figure 372Figure 372) as defined by the command;
    •   the NSID value selected by the Administrating Host for the Exported Namespace in the Exported
        Namespace ID (ENSID) field (refer to Figure 372Figure 372);
    •   the NSID for the Underlying Namespace in the Underlying Namespace ID (UNSID) field (refer to
        Figure 372Figure 372); and
    •   for a message-based controller:
            o   the controller identifier in the Underlying Controller ID (UCTRLID) field (refer to Figure
                372Figure 372); and
            o   the NQN value for the Underlying NVM Subsystem NQN (UNSNQN) field (refer to Figure
                372Figure 372).
If the Exported Namespace associated with an Underlying Namespace is not attached to an Exported
Controller in the specified Exported NVM Subsystem, then an Administrating Host is able to disassociate
that Underlying Namespace from the Exported NVM Subsystem by submitting a Manage Exported
Namespace command specifying:
    •   the Select field set to Disassociate Namespace (i.e., 02h);
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier in the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier (ESUBID) field
        (refer to Figure 370Figure 370) or the SUBNQN in the Exported NVM Subsystem NQN (ENSNQN)
        field (refer to Figure 373Figure 373) as defined by the command; and



                                                       637
                                                          NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   the NSID for the Exported Namespace in the Exported Namespace ID (ENSID) field (refer to Figure
        373Figure 373).
8.1.11.1.3 Managing the Configuration State for an Exported NVM Subsystem
Exported NVM Resources may require modification to their representation beyond what is provided when
an Exported NVM Subsystem is created (i.e., in addition to the Exported NVM Subsystem NVMe Qualified
Name, the Controller Identifiers and Namespace Identifiers that are specified when the resources are
associated). For example, to assist live migration of an NVM Subsystem (refer to Host Managed Live
Migration, section 8.1.14), the contents of data structures, log pages and features of NVM Resources in the
destination NVM Subsystem may need to be modified to match the corresponding content in the source
NVM Subsystem. Exported NVM Subsystems support this through an Exported NVM Subsystem Template.
An Exported NVM Subsystem Template allows an Administrating Host to modify, for one or more Exported
Controllers in an Exported NVM Subsystem,
    •   supported commands, log pages and features,
    •   data reported in Identify Controller data structures or Identify Namespace data structures,
    •   contents of log pages, and
    •   default, current and, optionally, saved values of features.
             Exported NVM Subsystem Template
An Underlying NVM Subsystem may support an Exported NVM Subsystem Template for use by Exported
NVM Subsystems. An Exported NVM Subsystem Template is identified by a UUID, and the support for a
particular Exported NVM Subsystem Template is indicated by the associated UUID being included in the
Exported NVM Subsystem Template UUID List (refer to section 5.2.14.2.23).
An Exported NVM Subsystem Template defines:
    •   the data structure used with the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send and Receive commands
        for sending and receiving the Exported NVM Subsystem Configuration State of the Exported NVM
        Subsystem resources;
    •   the data structure used with the Migration Send and Receive commands for sending and receiving
        the Exported NVM Subsystem State of Exported NVM Subsystem resources; and
    •   the capabilities of the Exported NVM Subsystem resources (i.e., supported commands, log pages
        and features).
8.1.11.1.4 Deleting an Exported NVM Subsystem
Prior to deleting an Exported NVM Subsystem, certain exported entities that are associated with that
Exported NVM Subsystem are required to be deleted as defined in section 5.2.19.1).
To delete an Exported NVM Subsystem, an Administrating host submits a Manage Exported NVM
Subsystem Send command (refer to section 5.2.19) with:
    •   the Select field set to Delete Exported NVM Subsystem (i.e., 1h); and
    •   specifies the Exported NVM Subsystem as defined in section 5.2.19).
8.1.11.1.5 Clearing all Exported NVM Subsystems
An Administrating host submits a Clear Exported NVM Resource Configuration command (refer to section
5.2.4) to delete all Exported NVM Subsystems (refer to Figure 723Figure 723).




                                                   638
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


                  Figure 723: Example steps for clearing all Exported NVM Subsystems

     Host




Upon successful completion of a Clear Exported NVM Resource Configuration command there are no
Exported NVM Subsystems. As a result of deleting any existing Exported NVM Subsystem, then all other
exported entities are also deleted: Exported Ports, Exported Controllers, and Exported Namespaces.
8.1.11.1.6 Firmware Update Restrictions
Refer to section 5.2.14.2.20 for guidelines and requirements on firmware updates that modify the contents
of the Exported NVM Subsystem Template UUID List defined in section 5.2.14.2.23. In addition, if:
    •   An Exported NVM Subsystem exists;
    •   that Exported NVM Subsystem has an Exported NVM Subsystem Template assigned; and
    •   the entry in the UUID list in the Exported NVM Subsystem Template UUID List for that Exported
        NVM Subsystem Template assigned does not contain the same UUID value in the same entry in
        the UUID list in the Exported NVM Subsystem Template UUID List in the firmware image requested
        to be activated by a Firmware Commit command,
then the controller shall abort that Firmware Commit command with a status code of Command Sequence
Error.
          Management of Exported NVM Resources for Memory-Based Transports
This section describes operations to Exported NVM Subsystems that are specific to memory-based
transports. Since the process deals with multiple hosts, those hosts are named according to Figure
721Figure 721.
8.1.11.2.1 Managing Exported Controllers
An Administrating Host uses the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command (refer to section
5.2.19) to specify the Exported Controllers to be associated with the specified Exported NVM Subsystem.
To assign a set of Underlying Controllers to that Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating Host submits
a Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command specifying:
    •   the Select field set to Associate Controllers (i.e., 05h);
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier Valid bit set to ‘1’ (refer to Figure 398Figure 398);
    •   the Management Operation Specific Identifier (MOSI) field set to the value of the Exported NVM
        Subsystem identifier for that Exported NVM Subsystem (refer to Figure 398Figure 398);
    •   the data buffer containing the list of Underlying Controllers to be associated with the specified
        Exported Controllers (refer to Figure 404Figure 404) in that Exported NVM Subsystem; and
    •   the Number of Dwords (NUMD) field set to the size of the data buffer.
There is no mechanism to remove the Exported Controllers from an Exported NVM Subsystem without
deleting that Exported NVM Subsystem. To remove the associations between the Underlying Controllers
to their corresponding Exported Controllers in an Exported NVM Subsystem, the Exported NVM Subsystem
must be deleted using:
    •   the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command specifying the Select field set to Delete
        (i.e., 01h); or
    •   the Clear Exported NVM Resource Configuration command (refer to section 5.2.4).



                                                      639
                                                           NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


The Administrating Host may use the Identify command specifying the CNS value 21h (i.e., Get Underlying
Controller List) to obtain the set of controllers within the NVM subsystem that are Underlying Controllers.
An Underlying Controller is only allowed to be assigned by the host to a single Exported NVM Subsystem.
Each specified Underlying Controller is required to be in a state where commands are not allowed to be
processed as described in section 5.2.19.1.5.
On successful completion of that Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command:
    •   those Underlying Controllers are assigned to the specified Exported NVM Subsystem; and
    •   Each Exported Controller associated with those Underlying Controllers is prohibited to report any
        information about Underlying NVM Subsystem resources or entities that is not associated with
        created Exported NVM Subsystem entities as described in section 8.1.11.
8.1.11.2.2 Configuring an Exported NVM Subsystem
This section describes methods for creating, configuring, and migrating an Exported NVM Subsystem.
             Method to creating an Exported NVM Subsystem
An Administrating Host is able to determine the Exported NVM Resources available within the Underlying
NVM Subsystem to be used to create an Exported NVM Subsystem by submitting:
    •   an Identify command specifying the CNS value of 1Dh to obtain the list of Underlying Namespaces
        within the Underlying NVM Subsystem (refer to section 5.2.14.2.20); and
    •   an Identify command specifying the CNS value of 21h to obtain the list of Underlying Controllers
        within the Underlying NVM Subsystem (refer to section 5.2.14.3.1).
An Administrating Host is able to determine the Exported NVM Resources currently allocated to existing
Exported NVM Subsystems:
    •   To obtain the Exported NVM Subsystems that exist within the Underlying NVM Subsystem by
        submitting a Manage Exported NVM Subsystem command specifying the List Exported NVM
        Subsystems management operation (i.e., Select field set to 01h, refer to section 5.2.18.1.2).
    •   For each existing Exported NVM Subsystem:
            o   Obtain the list of Exported Namespaces which are associated with an Underlying
                Namespace by submitting a Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command
                specifying the List Exported Namespaces management operation (i.e., Select field set to
                02h, refer to section 5.2.18.1.3); and
            o   Obtain the list of Exported Controllers which are associated with an Underlying Controller
                by submitting a Manage Exported NVM Subsystem command specifying the List Exported
                Controllers management operation (i.e., Select field set to 03h, refer to section 5.2.18.1.4).
To create the Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating Host submits a Manage Exported NVM
Subsystem Receive command as defined in section 8.1.11.1.1.
             Method to configure an Exported NVM Subsystem
For each Underlying Namespace to be associated with the Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating
Host submits a Manage Exported Namespace command specifying the Associate Namespace
management operation (refer to section 5.2.17.1.1 and section 8.1.11.1.2). The result is that an Exported
Namespace is created within that Exported NVM Subsystem.
The Administrating Host determines the set of Underlying Controllers to be associated with that Exported
NVM Subsystem. Once determined, those Underlying Controllers need to be in a condition where
commands are not being processed.
To associate that set of Underlying Controllers with that Exported NVM Subsystem, the Administrating Host
submits a Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command specifying the Associate Controllers
management operation (refer to section 5.2.19.1.5 and section 8.1.11.2.1). The result is that a set of
Exported Controllers exist within that Exported NVM Subsystem.



                                                    640
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If an Exported NVM Subsystem template was applied to the Exported NVM Subsystem when created (refer
to section 8.1.11.1.1), then the Administrating Host submits one or more Manage Exported NVM Subsystem
Send commands specifying the Set Exported Configuration State management operation (refer to section
5.2.19.1.6) and with the configurable parameters for that Exported NVM Subsystem in the command
(Command Dwords and data buffer) as defined by that Exported NVM Subsystem template.
The affected Underlying Controllers are disabled (e.g., the CC.EN bit is cleared to ‘0’ and the CSTS.RDY
bit is cleared to ‘0’) while Underlying Controllers are being associated with an Exported NVM Subsystem
(refer to section 5.2.19.1.5). Those Underlying Controllers should remain disabled when setting the
exported configuration state in that Exported NVM Subsystem (refer to section 5.2.21.2.4). If any affected
Underlying Controller performs processing while the exported configuration state is being set in that
Exported NVM subsystem (refer to section 5.2.21.2.4, then the effects of those two actions on processing
performed by that Underlying Controller are undefined (e.g., incomplete processing of one or more
commands, failure to post one or more command completions, one or more commands aborted with a
status code of Internal Error).
8.1.11.2.3 Migrating an Exported NVM Subsystem
This section describes how to migrate an Exported NVM Subsystem from one Underlying NVM Subsystem
to an Exported NVM Subsystem in a different Underlying NVM Subsystem. Since the migration of an
Exported NVM Subsystem involves multiple:
    •   Administrating Hosts;
    •   Underlying NVM Subsystems;
    •   Underlying Controllers;
    •   Underlying Namespaces;
    •   Exported NVM Subsystems;
    •   Exported Controllers; and
    •   Exported Namespaces,
the word “Source” is used to represent those entities interacting or contained in the Underlying NVM
Subsystem containing the Exported NVM Subsystem being migrated. The word “Destination” is used to
represent those entities interacting or contained in the Underlying NVM Subsystem to which the Exported
NVM Subsystem being migrated to.
The coordination between the Source Administrating Host and the Destination Administrating Host is
outside of scope for this specification. Note that the Source Administrating Host and the Destination
Administrating Host may be the same host if the migration is occurring in the same Underlying NVM
Subsystem.
             Creating the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem
The Destination Administrating Host creates the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem as defined in
section 8.1.11.2.2.1 the same way the Source Administrating Host created the Source Exported NVM
Subsystem. In this process the Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command returns:
    •   an Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier that identifies that Destination Exported NVM Subsystem
        in the Destination Underlying NVM Subsystem. That Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier has no
        relationship to the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem;
        and
    •   SUBNQN that identifies that Destination Exported NVM Subsystem in the Destination Underlying
        NVM Subsystem. That SUBNQN is unique and shall not have the same value as the SUBNQN
        returned to the Source Administrating Host at the time the Source Exported NVM Subsystem was
        created.
             Configuring the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem
The Destination Administrating Host creates the Underlying Namespaces in the Destination Underlying
NVM Subsystem. If the contents of the Source Underlying Namespaces are also being migrated with the
Source Exported NVM Subsystem, then it is the responsibility of the Source Administrating Host and the


                                                       641
                                                           NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


Destination Administrating Host to coordinate to cause the user data of each Underlying Namespace to be
migrated (refer to the method defined in section 8.1.14).
The Destination Administrating Host configures the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem as defined in
section 8.1.11.2.2.2 the same way the Source Administrating Host configured the Source Exported NVM
Subsystem with the following conditions:
    •   The Destination Exported NVM Subsystem has the same number of Exported Controllers as the
        Source Exported NVM Subsystem and those Destination Exported Controllers have the same
        controller identifiers as the Source Exported Controllers. The Destination Underlying Controllers
        are not required to have the same set of controller identifiers as the Source Underlying Controllers;
    •   The Destination Exported NVM Subsystem has the same number of Exported Namespaces as the
        Source Exported NVM Subsystem where the Destination Exported Namespaces have the same
        set of NSIDs as the Source Exported Namespaces. The Destination Underlying Namespaces are
        not required to have the same set of NSIDs as the Source Underlying Namespaces; and
    •   The Destination Exported NVM Subsystem template configurable parameters are set to the same
        values as set when configuring the Source Exported NVM Subsystem.
             Migrating the Source Exported NVM Subsystem State
The Exported NVM Subsystem template defines the Exported NVM Subsystem state data (migrated state
data), between the Source Exported NVM Subsystem and the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem;
therefore, refer to the definition of that Exported NVM Subsystem template. Refer to the NVM Express
Command Set Specification for the definition of the Reference Exported NVM Subsystem Template (i.e.,
identified by the UUID value BC33D0BB_764F42EE_84A27F92_3C21F01Fh).
The migration state data is allowed to be migrated by the host while the Exported Controllers in the Source
Exported NVM Subsystem are processing commands (i.e., live migration) by the Source Administrating
Host then submits one or more Migration Receive commands specifying:
    •   the Get Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation (i.e., 1h, refer to section
        5.2.20.1.2); and
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem,
to obtain the migration state data for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem.
The Source Administrating Host then transfers that migration state data to the Destination Administrating
Host to migrate that migration state data which is out of scope for this specification.
Once that migration state data is obtained by the Destination Administrating Host, the Destination
Administrating Host submits one or more Migration Send commands specifying:
    •   the Set Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation (i.e., 3h, refer to section
        5.2.21.2.4); and
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier for the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem,
to set the migration state data into the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem.
Once the Source Administrating Host wants to complete the migration of the final migration state data then
for each Source Exported Controller:
    •   The Source Administrating Host submits a Migration Send command specifying the Suspend
        management operation (i.e., 0h, refer to section 5.2.21.2.1) and that Source Underlying Controller
        that results in that Underlying Controller stopping the fetching of commands and to complete the
        processing of all previous fetched commands.
Upon all of the Source Underlying Controller being suspended (this is known as the start of the blackout for
the Source Exported NVM Subsystem) the Source Administrating Host then submits one or more Migration
Receive commands specifying:
    •   the Get Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation (i.e., 1h, refer to section
        5.2.20.1.2); and



                                                    642
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem,
to obtain the migration state data for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem.
The Source Administrating Host then transfers that migration state data to the Destination Administrating
Host to migrate that migration data which is out of scope for this specification.
Once that migration state data is obtained by the Destination Administrating Host, the Destination
Administrating Host submits one or more Migration Send commands specifying:
    •   the Set Exported NVM Subsystem State management operation (i.e., 3h, refer to section
        5.2.21.2.4); and
    •   the Exported NVM Subsystem Identifier for the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem,
to set the migration state data into the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem.
             Resuming the Destination Exported NVM Subsystem
For each Destination Exported Controller:
    •   the Destination Administrating Host submits a Migration Send command specifying the Resume
        management operation (i.e., 1h, refer to section 5.2.21.2.2) to the associated Destination
        Underlying Controller to resume command processing.
The end of the blackout for the Source Exported NVM Subsystem occurs when all of the Destination
Exported Controller resume operation.
          Management of Exported NVM Resources for Message-Based Transports (Informative)
Commands for managing Exported NVM Resources are processed by a controller in an Underlying NVM
Subsystem.
This section describes example flows to manage Exported NVM Resources through the use of the:
    •   Identify command with CNS set to 1Dh to retrieve the Underlying Namespace List;
    •   Identify command with CNS set to 1Eh to retrieve the list of Underlying Ports that may be used to
        export NVMe over Fabrics Subsystems;
    •   Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Receive command to create an Exported NVM Subsystem;
    •   Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command to manage access to an Exported NVM
        Subsystem;
    •   Manage Exported Namespace command to configure an Exported NVM Subsystem with
        namespaces;
    •   Manage Exported Port command to manage fabric port configurations on an Exported NVM
        Subsystem; and
    •   Manage Exported NVM Subsystem Send command to delete Exported NVM Subsystems.

8.1.12 Flexible Data Placement
           Flexible Data Placement Overview
The Flexible Data Placement (FDP) capability is an optional capability which allows the host to reduce write
amplification by aligning user data usage to physical media. The controller supports log pages which
indicate the status of FDP, statistics about the FDP operation, and information the host uses to detect and
correct usage patterns that increase write amplification.


                                                            647
                                                            NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


The scope of the Flexible Data Placement capability is an Endurance Group.
The host enables or disables Flexible Data Placement by issuing a Set Features command specifying the
Flexible Data Placement feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.21) and the FDP configuration (refer to section
5.2.13.1.29) to be applied to an Endurance Group. The host is required to delete all namespaces associated
with the specified Endurance Group before modifying the value of the Flexible Data Placement feature
(e.g., transitioning from disabled to enabled).
If a Set Features command specifies:
    •   the Flexible Data Placement feature;
    •   an Endurance Group in which one or more namespaces exist; and
    •   a different value from the current value of that feature for that Endurance Group,
then the controller shall abort the command with a status code of Command Sequence Error.
If a Set Features command is successful and changes the Feature value, then:
    •   all events in the FDP Events log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.32) are cleared; and
    •   all fields in the FDP Statistics log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.31) are cleared to 0h.
Refer to section 3.2.4 for the logical view of the non-volatile storage capacity for the Endurance Group with
Flexible Data Placement enabled.
The Namespace Management command (refer to section 8.1.17) is used to create a namespace within the
Endurance Group. All namespaces in an Endurance Group with Flexible Data Placement enabled shall be
associated with the NVM Command Set (refer to Figure 337Figure 337) (i.e., the Command Set Identifier
(CSI) field in the Namespace Management command shall be cleared to 00h). The capacity for the user
data stored by a write command to a namespace is allocated from the Reclaim Unit referenced by the
Reclaim Unit Handle and Reclaim Group specified by that write command. The user data for a namespace
is allowed to be in any stored Reclaim Unit within any Reclaim Group within the Endurance Group (refer to
Figure 15).
The Namespace Management command specifies a Placement Handle List (refer to the Namespace
Management command in the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification). Each entry in that
list specifies the Reclaim Unit Handle associated with the Placement Handle for that entry. The Placement
Handles are numbered from 0h to the number of entries in the list minus 1. Figure 729Figure 729 shows
an example where Namespace A associates Reclaim Unit Handle 1 with Placement Handle 0. A specific
Reclaim Unit Handle is not allowed to be associated with more than one Placement Handle per namespace.
There are no other requirements on which Reclaim Unit Handle is associated with which Placement Handle.
Namespaces are allowed to utilize the same (i.e., share) Reclaim Unit Handle but may have restrictions
defined in the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification.
The host is required to enable the Data Placement Directive (refer to section 8.1.9.4) to submit write
commands that specify a Placement Identifier (refer to Figure 296Figure 296 and Figure 297Figure 297) in
the DSPEC field. That Placement Identifier uniquely specifies the Reclaim Unit in which to place the user
data (refer to Figure 730Figure 730). The controller determines the Reclaim Unit by using the Reclaim Unit
Handle associated with the Placement Handle that was specified by the host when the namespace was
created. For example, if the write command in Figure 730Figure 730 specifies a Reclaim Group Identifier
value of 2h and a Placement Handle value of 1h, then the host is targeting the user data for that write
command to be placed into the Reclaim Unit associated with Reclaim Group 2h and Reclaim Unit Handle
NRUH-1.
A Placement Identifier is invalid if:
    •   the Reclaim Group Identifier value is greater than or equal to the number of Reclaim Groups
        supported by the enabled FDP configuration (refer to the NRG field in Figure 294Figure 294); or
    •   the Placement Handle is greater than or equal to the number of Placement Handles supported by
        the Namespace Management command of the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set
        specification.



                                                     648
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If the Placement Identifier in the DSPEC field of a write command is invalid, then the controller shall:
    •       select the Reclaim Group and Reclaim Unit Handle accessible by the specified namespace to
            determine the placement of the user data for that write command; and
    •       generate an Invalid Placement Identifier FDP Event if that event is enabled for the selected Reclaim
            Unit Handle. To receive the FDP event, the host should enable the Invalid Placement Identifier FDP
            Event on all Reclaim Unit Handles.
Any write command to a namespace that exists in an Endurance Group with Flexible Data Placement
enabled that does not specify the Data Placement Directive uses the Placement Handle value 0h and the
controller selects the Reclaim Group for that command. For example, if the write command does not specify
the Data Placement Directive, then, as illustrated in Figure 730Figure 730, Placement Handle value of 0h
is associated with Reclaim Unit Handle 1h and the controller may place the user data into the Reclaim Unit
associated any Reclaim Group using Reclaim Unit Handle 1h.

A write command that places user data into a Reclaim Unit causes reduction of the remaining capacity of
that Reclaim Unit. If that Reclaim Unit is written to capacity, then the controller modifies the Reclaim Unit
Handle referencing that Reclaim Unit to reference a different Reclaim Unit within the same Reclaim Group.
A controller may modify a Reclaim Unit Handle to reference a different Reclaim Unit as part of performing
a sanitize operation (refer to section 8.1.27).
A Reclaim Unit shall only be referenced by one Reclaim Unit Handle. Therefore, a write command that
utilizes a Reclaim Unit Handle results in the user data from that write command being initially isolated from



                                                                    649
                                                            NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


the user data from any other write command that utilizes a different Reclaim Unit Handle. Each Reclaim
Unit Handle has a type as defined in Figure 295Figure 295 that identifies the isolation requirements of the
user data moved by the controller to a different Reclaim Unit due to vendor specific controller operations
(e.g., garbage collection).
A controller is allowed to move user data that was written by the host that utilized a Reclaim Unit Handle
with an Initially Isolated type (refer to Figure 295Figure 295) to a different Reclaim Unit within the same
Reclaim Group. In addition, the controller is allowed to move user data written by the host that utilized
different Reclaim Unit Handles with an Initially Isolated type to that different Reclaim Unit within the same
Reclaim Group as shown in Figure 731Figure 731.
A controller is allowed to move user data that was written by the host that utilized a Reclaim Unit Handle
with a Persistently Isolated type (refer to Figure 295Figure 295) to a different Reclaim Unit within the same
Reclaim Group. However, the controller shall only move user data written by the host that utilized the same
Reclaim Unit Handles with a Persistently Isolated type to the different Reclaim Unit within the same Reclaim
Group as shown in Figure 732Figure 732.

The result of a Namespace Management command that creates a namespace within the Endurance Group
that has FDP enabled is that at least one Placement Handle is defined for that namespace (refer to the
Namespace Management section in applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification).
For any namespace created in an Endurance Group that has Flexible Data Placement enabled, the host
may issue an I/O Management Receive command to obtain a list of Placement Handles and the associated
Reclaim Unit Handles that are used by the Data Placement Directive in write commands.
If the Flexible Data Placement capability is supported, then the controller shall support the following:
    a) the Feature Identifiers Supported and Effects log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.18);


                                                     650
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


   b) the I/O Management Receive command (refer to section 7.3) and the Reclaim Unit Handle Status
      Management Operation in that command (refer to Figure 651Figure 651);
   c) the I/O Management Send command (refer to section 7.4) and the Placement Identifier Update
      Management Operation in that command (refer to Figure 655Figure 655);
   d) the Flexible Data Placement feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.21);
   e) the FDP Configurations log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.29);
   f) the Reclaim Unit Handle Usage log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.30);
   g) the FDP Statistics log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.31);
   h) the Flexible Data Placement Events feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.22);
   i) the FDP Events log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.32); and
   j) the Data Placement Directive (refer to section 8.1.9.4).
         Enabling Flexible Data Placement (Informative)
The host prepares an Endurance Group for operation in Flexible Data Placement using the following
process:
   1) Validate that the Flexible Data Placement capability is supported by issuing an Identify command
      to access the Identify Controller data structure and checking that the Flexible Data Placement
      Support (FDPS) bit is set to ‘1’.
   2) Delete any existing namespaces that exist in the Endurance Group where Flexible Data Placement
      is to be enabled.
   3) Issue a Get Log Page command specifying the FDP Configurations log page (refer to section
      5.2.13.1.29). Parse the FDP Configurations List in the returned log page to determine the desired
      FDP configuration.
   4) Enable Flexible Data Placement utilizing that desired FDP configuration by issuing a Set Features
      command specifying:
           a. the Flexible Data Placement feature;
           b. the Endurance Group Identifier field set to the ENDGID of the Endurance Group in which
              Flexible Data Placement is to be enabled;
           c. the FDPE bit set to ‘1’ (i.e., enabling Flexible Data Placement); and
           d. the Flexible Data Placement Configuration Index field set to the index of the desired FDP
              configuration from the FDP Configurations List in the FDP Configurations log page.
   5) Issue an Identify command specifying the Identify Namespace data structure (i.e., CNS 00h as
      defined in Figure 336Figure 336) to identify which LBA formats are supported.
   6) For each namespace to be created in the Endurance Group, issue a Namespace Management
      command (refer to section 5.2.25) specifying:
           a. the Select field set to the Create operation;
           b. the User Data Format; and
           c. the Placement Handle List used to define the Reclaim Unit Handle associated with each
              Placement Handle of the namespace (refer to the Namespace Management section of the
              applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specification).
   7) Issue Get Features commands for the FDP Events feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.22) to acquire
      the list of supported FDP events and the enabled state of each supported FDP event.
   8) Issue Set Features commands for the FDP Events feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.22) to specify
      if FDP events are required for Reclaim Unit Handles.
   9) For each namespace created in an Endurance Group in which the Data Placement Directive is to
      be utilized by the host by write commands specifying that namespace:
           a. Issue a Directive Send command specifying:
                    i.   the Directive Operation field set to Enable Directive (i.e., 01h);
                   ii.   the NSID of that namespace;
                  iii.   the DTYPE field in Command Dword 11 set to Identify (i.e., 00h);
                  iv.    the DTYPE field in Command Dword 12 set to Data Placement (i.e., 02h); and
                   v.    the Enable Directive bit set to ‘1’ (i.e., to enable the Data Placement Directive).


                                                         651
                                                            NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


            b. Issue an Identify command with CNS value 08h (i.e., the I/O Command Set Independent
               Identify Namespace data structure) to determine if a volatile write cache is present for the
               namespace.
Following a Controller Level Reset, the host performs the following actions before resuming use of Flexible
Data Placement in an Endurance Group:
    1) Determine the FDP configuration:
            a. Issue a Get Feature command specifying the Flexible Data Placement feature (i.e., 1Dh)
               and the ENDGID for the Endurance Group to determine if Flexible Data Placement is
               enabled and the Flexible Data Placement Configuration Index.
            b. Issue a Get Log Page command specifying the FDP Configurations log page (i.e., Log
               Page Identifier 20h).
    2) Issue Get Features commands for the FDP Events feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.22) to acquire
       the list of supported FDP events and the enabled state of each supported FDP event.
    3) Issue Set Features commands for the FDP Events feature (refer to section 5.2.30.1.22) to specify
       if supported FDP events are required for Reclaim Unit Handles.
    4) For each namespace in the Endurance Group that the Data Placement Directive is to be utilized
       by the host by write commands specifying that namespace:
            a. Issue an I/O Management Receive command to determine the Placement Handles for that
               namespace; and
            b. Issue an Identify command with CNS value 08h (i.e., the I/O Command Set Independent
               Identify Namespace data structure) to determine if a volatile write cache is present for the
               namespace.
          Write Commands using Flexible Data Placement (Informative)
Hosts writing user data to a namespace created in an Endurance Group that has Flexible Data Placement
enabled have two mechanisms for specifying the placement of the user data with the Endurance Group to
the controller.
  1.    Each namespace has a default Placement Handle. If any write command:
            a. has the DTYPE field being ignored by the controller (refer to section 8.1.9.4); or
            b. has the DTYPE field not being ignored by the controller and specifies a DTYPE field value
               cleared to 00h,
        then the Placement Handle value of 0h for the specified namespace is combined with a Reclaim
        Group selected by the controller to create the Placement Identifier (refer to Figure 296Figure 296
        and Figure 297Figure 297) utilized for that write command.
  2.    If any write command has the DTYPE field not being ignored by the controller and specifies a
        DTYPE field set to Data Placement (i.e., 02h) and specifies a namespace in which the Data
        Placement Directive is enabled, then the Placement Identifier specified by the DSPEC field
        specifies the Reclaim Group Identifier and Placement Handle used for the write command.
To reduce write amplification, hosts track the user data written to an entire Reclaim Unit and deallocate that
user data by issuing one or more Dataset Management commands specifying the AD bit set to ‘1’ and one
or more Range fields specifying the LBA ranges that were written to that Reclaim Unit.
8.1.13 Host-Initiated Refresh Operation
The Host-Initiated Refresh operation of the Device Self-test command performs implementation-specific
refresh operations that verify the media integrity and ensure access to media (e.g., media in an NVM
subsystem that has not been in operation for a long period of time and/or has been subject to extreme
environmental conditions). Examples of refresh operations may include read verification, rewrite of
underlying media that are exhibiting a high correctable error rate (e.g., to prevent future errors), and other
maintenance activities. A Host-Initiated Refresh operation does not change stored user data.




                                                     652
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


If the Host-Initiated Refresh operation is supported, then the controller shall set the HIRS bit to ‘1’ in the
DSTO field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
The percentage complete of the Host-Initiated Refresh operation is indicated in the Current Percentage
Complete field in the Device Self-test log page (refer to section 5.2.13.1.7).
For Host-Initiated Refresh operation, the NSID field in the Device Self-test command is ignored by the
controller and all media in the NVM subsystem is refreshed regardless of whether any portion of the media
is or is not part of any namespace.
A Host-Initiated Refresh operation shall be aborted:
    a)   if any Controller Level Reset affects the controller on which the device self-test is being performed;
    b)   if a Format NVM command is processed by any controller in the NVM subsystem;
    c)   if a sanitize operation is started (refer to section 5.2.26); or
    d)   if a Device Self-test command with the Self-Test Code field set to Fh is processed by any controller
         in the NVM subsystem.
A Controller Level Reset on a controller that is not performing the Host-Initiated Refresh operation shall not
impact that Host-Initiated Refresh operation.
8.1.14 Host Managed Live Migration
The migration of a controller, by a host that is using the Host Managed Live Migration capability involves
one or more NVM subsystems, multiple hosts, and multiple controllers. In this section, to differentiate
between the multiple hosts and controllers, each is given a unique name as illustrated in Figure 733Figure
733. In an NVM subsystem that supports Host Managed Live Migration, each controller that sets the
HMLMS bit to ‘1’ is referred to as a Migration Management Controller (MMC) and each host associated
with an MMC is referred to as a Migration Management Host (MMH). In that same NVM subsystem, all
other controllers (i.e., those that clear the HMLMS bit to ‘0’) are referred to as Migratable Controllers.
The Host Managed Live Migration capability allows an MMH to use an MMC to migrate a Migratable
Controller from a Source NVM Subsystem to a Migratable Controller in a Destination NVM Subsystem.
During that migration, a host is actively submitting commands to a Migratable Controller in the Source NVM
Subsystem and that controller is processing those commands.
The MMH that is managing the migration of a Migratable Controller from the Source NVM Subsystem is
responsible for ensuring that the Migratable Controller in the Destination NVM Subsystem is compatible
with controller state of the Migratable Controller from the Source NVM Subsystem. It is also the
responsibility of the MMH to transfer the migrating data between the NVM subsystems.




                                                         653
                                                                                 NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4

An MMC is an I/O controller or an Administrative controller that supports the Host Managed Live Migration
capability and provides the ability for the MMH to use privileged actions (refer to section 3.10) to:
     •      suspend the processing of commands on the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem
            being migrated (refer to the Migration Send command in section 5.2.21.2.1);
     •      obtain the state of the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem being migrated (refer
            to the Migration Receive command in section 5.2.20.1.1);
     •      set that controller state in the Migratable Controller in the Destination NVM Subsystem (refer to
            the Migration Send command in section 5.2.21.2.3); and
     •      resume the operation on the Migratable Controller in the Destination NVM Subsystem (refer to the
            Migration Send command in section 5.2.21.2.2).
A controller indicates support for the Host Managed Live Migration capability by setting the Host Managed
Live Migration Support (HMLMS) bit to ‘1’ in the Optional Admin Command Support (OACS) field in the
Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).

An MMC is not permitted to be migrated and:
    •      shall support:
           •      the Migration Send command with the Management Operations:
                         o     Suspend (i.e., 0h);
                         o     Resume (i.e., 1h); and
                         o     Set Controller State (i.e., 2h);
           •      the Migration Receive command with the Management Operations:
                         o     Get Controller State (i.e., 1h);
                  and
           •      the CNS value of 20h in the Identify command (i.e., Supported Controller State Formats data
                  structure (refer to section 5.2.14.2.22)).
If the NVM subsystem contains one or more Migration Management Controllers, then:




                                                                       654
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


    •   each controller (i.e., MMC and Migratable Controller) in that NVM subsystem does not support the
        Host Memory Buffer (refer to the Host Memory Buffer Preferred Size (HMPRE) field in the Identify
        Controller data structure in Figure 338Figure 338); and
    •   each Migratable Controller in that NVM subsystem is allowed to be migrated and shall not support:
            o   the Migration Send command (refer to section 5.2.21);
            o   the Migration Receive command (refer to section 5.2.17);
            o   the CNS value of 20h in the Identify command (i.e., returning Supported Controller State
                Formats data structure (refer to section 5.2.14.2.22)); and
            o   the Controller Data Queue command with the Create Queue management operation
                specifying the User Data Migration Queue (refer to section 5.2.5.1.1).
A Controller Level Reset on an MMC shall cause that MMC to:
    •   delete all User Data Migration Queues on that MMC; and
    •   stop tracking all host memory changes on that MMC.
A Controller Level Reset on a Migratable Controller shall cause that Migratable Controller to:
    •   remove a suspended state if that Migratable Controller is suspended by a Migration Send command
        specifying the Suspend management operation (refer to section 5.2.21.2.1); and
    •   retain any persistent controller state that has been committed to that Migratable Controller from a
        Migration Send command specifying the Set Controller State management operation (refer to
        section 5.2.21.2.3).
During the migration of a Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem while that Migratable
Controller is processing commands, it may be necessary for the MMHS to obtain the user data
modifications to namespaces attached to that Migratable Controller and modifications made by that
Migratable Controller to host memory in the host. The Track Send command (refer to section 5.2.32) and
the Track Receive command (refer to section 5.2.31) allows the host to use privileged actions (refer to
section 3.10) to:
    •   determine user data in namespaces attached to a controller that has changed; and
    •   determine host memory that has changed due to commands processed by a controller.
A controller indicates support for tracking changes to user data in namespaces attached to a controller by
setting the Track User Data Changes Support (TUDCS) bit to ‘1’ in the Tracking Attributes (TRATTR) field
in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
A controller indicates support for tracking changes to host memory (refer to section 1.5.48) due to the
processing of commands by a controller by setting the Track Host Memory Changes Support (THMCS) bit
to ‘1’ in the TRATTR field.
         Process for Migrating a Controller
This section provides an example sequence of steps to allow the MMHS to migrate a Migratable Controller
in the Source NVM Subsystem and the attached namespaces to a Migratable Controller in the Destination
NVM Subsystem (refer to Figure 733Figure 733). Additionally, the steps include obtaining the host memory
modifications made to the host due to the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem processing
commands during the migration.
In this example the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem has:
    •   the Track User Data Changes Support (TUDCS) bit set to ‘1’ in the Tracking Attributes (TRATTR)
        field in the Identify Controller data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338); and
    •   the Track Host Memory Changes Support (THMCS) bit set to ‘1’ in the Tracking Attributes
        (TRATTR) field in the Identify Controller data structure.
If attached namespaces are not required to be migrated by the MMHS, then those steps may be ignored.
If host memory modifications are not required to be obtained by the MMHS, then those steps may be
ignored.



                                                        655
                                                       NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


1. The MMHS copies (i.e., migrates) the user data in namespaces attached to the Migratable
   Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem while the host is submitting commands and the
   Migratable Controller is processing those submitted commands.
   a. The MMHS creates a User Data Migration Queue in the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem
      by submitting a Controller Data Queue command to that MMC (refer to section 5.2.4)
      specifying:
        •   the Select field set to the Create Controller Data Queue (i.e., 0h);
        •   the Queue Type field set to User Data Migration Queue; and
        •   the Controller Identifier field (refer to Figure 172) set to the controller identifier for the
            Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem.
   b. If the Controller Data Queue command is successful, the completion queue entry contains the
      Controller Data Queue Identifier for the created User Data Migration Queue. The MMHS
      causes the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem to post user data modifications to namespaces
      attached to the Migratable Controller by submitting a Track Send command (refer to section
      5.2.32) to that MMC specifying:
        •   the Select field set to Log User Data Changes (i.e., 0h);
        •   the Logging Action bit set to ‘1’ (i.e., start logging); and
        •   the Controller Data Queue Identifier field set to the Controller Data Queue Identifier from
            the completion queue entry for the Controller Data Queue command.
        It is the responsibility of the MMHS to make sure that the User Data Migration Queue is sized
        properly and there may be more restrictions on that MMHS as specified by the appropriate I/O
        command set (e.g., the NVM Command Set requires the MMHS to not allow the User Data
        Migration Queue to become full). Refer to section 8.1.7 for a description of the User Data
        Migration Queue (i.e., a Controller Data Queue).
   c.   If the Track Send command is successful, then the MMHS starts copying the namespaces
        attached to the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem to the Destination NVM
        Subsystem. Refer to the applicable NVM Express I/O Command Set specifications for
        capabilities that may reduce the amount of user data that is required to copied (e.g., the Get
        LBA Status command in the NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification).
2. The MMHS causes the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem to start tracking the modifications to
   host memory in the host due to the Migratable Controller processing submitted commands.
   a. The MMHS submits a Track Send command to the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem (refer
      to section 5.2.32) specifying:
        •   the Select field set to the Track Memory Changes (i.e., 1h);
        •   the Tracking Action (TACT) bit set to ‘1’;
        •   the Controller Identifier field specifying the identifier for the Migratable Controller in the
            Source NVM Subsystem being migrated; and
        •   a Track Memory Changes data structure in the data buffer specifying the host memory to
            be tracked as described by the set of host memory ranges.
   b. If the Track Send command is successful, then the MMHS may query the host memory
      modifications that have resulted from the Migratable Controller processing commands by
      submitting a Track Receive command (refer to section 5.2.31) to the MMC in the Source NVM
      Subsystem specifying:
        •   the Select field set to the Tracked Memory Changes (i.e., 0h); and
        •   the Controller Identifier field specifying the identifier for the Migratable Controller in the
            Source NVM Subsystem being migrated.
3. Once the MMHS has copied the namespaces attached to the Migratable Controller in the Source
   NVM Subsystem, that MMHS determines a time to suspend that Migratable Controller. During this
   period, that MMHS is migrating the user data in the namespaces attached to that Migratable



                                                656
NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


      Controller that are identified in the posted entries in the User Data Migration Queue. That MMHS
      may handle the modified host memory in the host as reported by the Track Receive command.
   4. The MMHS suspends the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem by submitting a
      Migration Send command to the MMC in the Source NVM Subsystem specifying:
            •   the Select field set to the Suspend (i.e., 0h);
            •   the Suspend Type field set to Suspend (i.e., 1h);
            •   Delete User Data Migration Queue bit set to ‘1’, if the MMHS desires that the MMC delete
                the User Data Migration Queue being used to log user data changes of the Migratable
                Controller being migrated; and
            •   the Controller Identifier field (refer to Figure 423Figure 423) set to the controller identifier
                for the Migratable Controller to be suspended (i.e., the Migratable Controller being
                migrated).
       Prior to completing that Migration Send command:
           •    the specified Migratable Controller being suspended:
                o     stops fetching commands (i.e., from the Admin queue and I/O queues); and
                o     completes all previously fetched commands;
                and
           •    the MMC processing that Migration Send command:
                o     if user data is being logged into a User Data Migration Queue that is associated with
                      the Migratable Controller being migrated, an entry is placed into the User Data
                      Migration Queue that indicates the user data logging has suspended, and then deletes
                      the User Data Migration Queue, if the Delete User Data Migration Queue bit is set to
                      ‘1’.
   5. Since the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM Subsystem is suspended, the MMHS migrates
      the user data in the namespaces attached to the Migratable Controller that are identified in the
      posted entries in the User Data Migration Queue. Refer to the applicable NVM Express I/O
      Command Set specification to determine how the entries identify when entries have completed
      being posted. That MMHS may handle the modified host memory in the host as reported by the
      Track Receive command.
   6. The MMHS is able to obtain the controller state of the Migratable Controller in the Source NVM
      Subsystem by submitting one or more Migration Receive commands to the MMC in the Source
      NVM Subsystem specifying:
       a. the Select field set to the Get Controller State (i.e., 0h);
       b. the Sequence Indicator field set to the proper sequence value;
       c. the Controller Identifier field set to the controller identifier for the Migratable Controller in the
          Source NVM Subsystem;
       d. the Controller State Version Index field set to an index into the NVMe Controller State Version
          list in the Supported Controller State Formats data structure for MMC in the Source NVM
          Subsystem (refer to Figure 358Figure 358) if the NVMe defined controller state is required; and
       e. the Controller State UUID Index field set to an index in the Vendor Specific Controller State
          UUID Supported list in the Supported Controller State Formats Data Structure for MMC in the
          Source NVM Subsystem (refer to Figure 358Figure 358), if vendor specific controller state is
          required.
   7. After the MMHS has transferred the obtained controller state information to the MMHD, the MMHD
      sets that controller state into a Migratable Controller by submitting a sequence of one or more
      Migration Send commands to the MMC in the Destination NVM Subsystem specifying:
           •    the Select field set to Set Controller State (i.e., 2h);
           •    the Sequence Indicator field set to the proper sequence value;
           •    the Controller Identifier field set to the controller identifier for the Migratable Controller in
                the Destination NVM Subsystem;


                                                          657
                                                              NVM Express® Base Specification, Revision 2.4


             •    the Controller State Version Index field set to an index into the NVMe Controller State
                  Version list in the Supported Controller State Formats data structure for MMC in the
                  Destination NVM Subsystem (refer to Figure 358Figure 358) if value of the NVMe
                  Controller State Size (NVMECSS) field is non-zero (refer to Figure 431Figure 431); and
             •    the Controller State UUID Index field set to an index in the Vendor Specific Controller State
                  UUID Supported list in the Supported Controller State Formats Data Structure for MMC in
                  the Source NVM Subsystem (refer to Figure 358Figure 358), if the value of the Vendor
                  Specific Size (VSS) field is non-zero (refer to Figure 431Figure 431).
    8. The MMHD resumes operation on the Migratable Controller in the Destination NVM Subsystem
       (i.e., the migrated controller) by submitting a Migration Send command to the MMC in the
       Destination NVM Subsystem specifying:
             •    the Select field set to Resume (i.e., 1h); and
             •    the Controller Identifier field (refer to Figure 424Figure 424) set to the controller identifier
                  for the Migratable Controller to be resumed.
8.1.15 Key Per I/O
The Key Per I/O capability provides a mechanism to use encryption keys that have been injected into an
NVM subsystem by a host. The mechanism to perform activation of the Key Per I/O capability, encryption
key injection, management, and association to encryption key tag is outside the scope of this specification.
One mechanism is defined in the TCG Storage Security Subsystem Class: Key Per I/O Specification using
the NVMe Admin commands Security Send and Security Receive. If the TCG mechanism is used, any
additional modifications to the NVM subsystem as a result of activation of the Key Per I/O Security Provider
are defined in the TCG Storage Interface Interactions Specification (SIIS).
Encryption keys injected into the NVM subsystem may be referenced by I/O commands through the use of
the encryption key tag (refer to the KEYTAG field in Figure 734Figure 734) associated with the encryption
keys. If an I/O command CETYPE field is set to the KPIOTAG value, then the CEV field (refer to Figure
734Figure 734) of that I/O command specifies the encryption key tag associated with the encryption key to
be used to encrypt or decrypt the data in that I/O command. The association of an encryption key tag to a
specific encryption key is outside the scope of this specification. One association mechanism is defined in
the TCG Storage Security Subsystem Class: Key Per I/O Specification.
The Key Per I/O Scope bit (refer to Figure 338Figure 338) indicates if the Key Per I/O capability:
    •     applies to all read and write commands in all namespaces within the NVM subsystem; or
    •     independently applies to read and write commands in each namespace within the NVM subsystem.
The Key Per I/O capability does not have any effect on host accesses to RPMBs and Boot Partitions as
these features are not addressed through I/O commands that specify a namespace.
A controller that supports the Key Per I/O capability shall set the KPIOS bit to ‘1’ in the Identify Controller
data structure (refer to Figure 338Figure 338).
A namespace that supports the Key Per I/O capability shall set the KPIOSNS bit to ‘1’ in the I/O Command
Set Independent Identify Namespace data structure (refer to Figure 346Figure 346).
The Key Per I/O capability uses the Command Extension Type (CETYPE) and Command Extension Value
(CEV) fields in all read and write commands. Definition of the CETYPE field values are shown in Figure
734Figure 734.

                                       that identifies the encryption key used to encrypt or decrypt the data of the
